sentences.zh: 羅倫，字彜正，吉安永豐人。

translations.literal: Luo Lun, styled Yizheng, was a native of Yongfeng in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Lun, styled Yizheng, was from Yongfeng in Ji'an prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五歲嘗隨母入園，果落，眾競取，倫獨賜而後受。

translations.literal: At age five he once followed his mother into a garden; when fruit fell, everyone scrambled to take it, but Lun alone waited until it was given to him before accepting.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five, he once went into a garden with his mother. Fruit fell, and everyone rushed to grab it; Lun alone waited until it was offered to him before he took any.

sentences.zh: 家貧樵牧，挾書誦不輟。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he gathered firewood and herded, yet carried books and recited without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor and he had to cut wood and tend herds, he always carried books with him and never stopped reading aloud.

sentences.zh: 及為諸生，誌聖賢學，嘗曰：「舉業非能壞人，人自壞之耳。

translations.literal: When he became a student, he set his mind on the learning of sages and worthies and once said: "Examination studies cannot ruin a man; a man ruins himself."
translations.idiomatic: After he became a licentiate, he devoted himself to the learning of the sages and once remarked, "Civil-service examination work cannot ruin a man—it is only that men ruin themselves."

sentences.zh: 」知府張瑄憫其貧，周之粟，謝不受。

translations.literal: " The prefect Zhang Xuan pitied his poverty and supplied him grain; he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The prefect Zhang Xuan, taking pity on his poverty, sent him grain, but he politely refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 居父母喪，逾大祥，始食鹽酪。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his parents, only after passing the daxiang period did he begin to eat salted foods and dairy.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents, he did not touch salted food or dairy until after the daxiang observance had ended.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，廷試，對策萬余言。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua, at the palace examination he submitted a policy response of more than ten thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: In 1466, at the palace examination, he submitted a policy response of more than ten thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 直斥時弊，名震都下。

translations.literal: He directly denounced the abuses of the age, and his name shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced current abuses forthrightly, and his name resounded throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第一，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: He was selected as top jinshi and appointed Hanlin Academician Editor.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed first among the jinshi and appointed Hanlin Academician Editor.

sentences.zh: 逾二月，大學士李賢奔喪畢，奉詔還朝。

translations.literal: After more than two months, Grand Secretary Li Xian, having completed his rush home for mourning, received an edict to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later, Grand Secretary Li Xian, having finished the mourning rush for his parent, was ordered by imperial edict to return to court.

sentences.zh: 倫詣賢沮之，不聽。

translations.literal: Lun went to Xian to dissuade him, but Xian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lun went to Li Xian to dissuade him, but Li would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞朝廷援楊溥故事，起復大學士李賢。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the court, citing the precedent of Yang Pu, has recalled Grand Secretary Li Xian from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the court, invoking the precedent of Yang Pu, has recalled Grand Secretary Li Xian from mourning service.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂賢大臣，起復大事，綱常風化系焉，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that Xian is a great minister, and recall from mourning is a great matter on which the cardinal norms and transforming influence of custom depend; it cannot be treated without caution.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that Li Xian is a great minister, and recalling a minister from mourning is a matter on which the cardinal norms and moral customs of the realm depend; it must be handled with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 曩陛下制策有曰：「朕夙夜拳拳，欲正大綱，舉萬目，使人倫明於上，風俗厚於下。

translations.literal: Formerly, in Your Majesty's examination questions, it was said: "I day and night earnestly desire to rectify the great norms, raise up every eye, and make human relations clear above and customs thick below."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once wrote in the examination questions: "I work earnestly day and night to set right the great norms, to lift up every standard of conduct, and to make human relations clear at court and customs sound among the people."

sentences.zh: 」竊謂明人倫，厚風俗，莫先於孝。

translations.literal: " Your subject ventures to say that to clarify human relations and thicken customs, nothing comes before filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: " I believe that to clarify human relations and strengthen customs, nothing comes before filial piety.

sentences.zh: 在禮，子有父母之喪，君三年不呼其門。

translations.literal: According to ritual, when a son is in mourning for his parents, the ruler for three years does not call at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: According to the rites, when a son is mourning his parents, the ruler for three years does not summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 子夏問：「三年之喪，金革無避，禮歟？

translations.literal: Zixia asked: "For the three-year mourning, there is no avoiding arms and armor—is this ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: Zixia asked Confucius: "For the three-year mourning, must one not avoid military service—is that what the rites require?"

sentences.zh: 」孔子曰：「魯公伯禽有為為之也。

translations.literal: " Confucius said: "Duke Bo Qin of Lu had someone act to bring this about."
translations.idiomatic: " Confucius replied: "It was because Duke Bo Qin of Lu had someone arrange it that way."

sentences.zh: 今以三年之喪從其利者，吾弗知也。

translations.literal: As for one who now, during the three-year mourning, follows his own advantage, I do not understand him."
translations.idiomatic: As for those who now, during the three-year mourning, follow their own advantage instead—I do not understand them at all."

sentences.zh: 」陛下於賢，以為金革之事起復之歟？

translations.literal: " Does Your Majesty regard Xian as recalled for arms-and-armor affairs?
translations.idiomatic: " Does Your Majesty believe that Li Xian is being recalled for urgent military affairs?

sentences.zh: 則未之有也。

translations.literal: If so, there is no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: If so, there is no such emergency.

sentences.zh: 以大臣起復之歟？

translations.literal: Or is he recalled as a great minister?
translations.idiomatic: Or is he being recalled simply because he is a great minister?

sentences.zh: 則禮所未見也。

translations.literal: If so, ritual has never seen such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: If so, the rites know no such precedent.

sentences.zh: 夫為人君，當舉先王之禮教其臣；

translations.literal: For one who is ruler, he ought to raise up the rites of the former kings to teach his ministers;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler ought to uphold the rites of the former kings to instruct his ministers;

sentences.zh: 為人臣，當守先王之禮事其君。

translations.literal: for one who is minister, he ought to keep the rites of the former kings in serving his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: and a minister ought to observe the rites of the former kings in serving his ruler.

sentences.zh: 昔宋仁宗嘗起復富弼矣，弼辭曰：「不敢遵故事以遂前代之非，但當據《禮經》以行今日之是。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Renzong of Song once recalled Fu Bi from mourning; Bi declined, saying: "I dare not follow precedent to perpetuate the wrong of a former age, but should act according to the Classic of Rites to perform what is right today."
translations.idiomatic: In the past, Emperor Renzong of Song once tried to recall Fu Bi from mourning. Bi declined, saying, "I dare not follow precedent merely to perpetuate a former age's error; I should act according to the Classic of Rites and do what is right today."

sentences.zh: 」仁宗卒從其請。

translations.literal: " In the end Renzong followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Renzong granted his request.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘗起復劉珙矣，珙辭曰：「身在草土之中，國無門庭之寇，難冒金革之名，私竊利祿之實。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong once recalled Liu Gong from mourning; Gong declined, saying: "My person is amid grass and earth; the state has no enemy at the gate; it is hard to take the name of arms and armor, yet privately to seize the substance of salary and emolument."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong once tried to recall Liu Gong from mourning. Gong declined, saying, "My body is still amid grass and earth in mourning; the state has no enemy at its gates. It would be hard to claim the exemption for military emergency while privately grasping salary and rank."

sentences.zh: 」孝宗不抑其情。

translations.literal: " Xiaozong did not restrain his feeling.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaozong did not override his wishes.

sentences.zh: 此二君者，未嘗以故事強其臣。

translations.literal: These two rulers never used precedent to compel their ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Neither of these rulers ever forced a minister with precedent alone.

sentences.zh: 二臣者。

translations.literal: These two ministers
translations.idiomatic: Neither of these ministers

sentences.zh: 未嘗以故事徇其君。

translations.literal: never used precedent to indulge their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: ever yielded to his ruler merely because of precedent.

sentences.zh: 故史冊書之為盛事，士大夫傳之為美談。

translations.literal: Therefore the historical records wrote of it as a grand affair, and scholar-officials transmitted it as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the histories record these episodes as great events and scholar-officials still recount them as exemplary stories.

sentences.zh: 無他，君能教臣以孝，臣有孝可移於君也。

translations.literal: There is nothing else to it: the ruler could teach his ministers through filial piety, and the ministers had filial piety that could be transferred to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is simple: the ruler could teach his ministers through filial piety, and the ministers had filial piety that could be offered up to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 自是而後，無復禮義。

translations.literal: From this time onward, ritual and righteousness were no more.
translations.idiomatic: After that, ritual and righteousness were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 王黼、史嵩之、陳宜中、賈似道之徒，皆援故事起復。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, Shi Songzhi, Chen Yizhong, Jia Sidao, and the like all cited precedent in recall from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Wang Fu, Shi Songzhi, Chen Yizhong, and Jia Sidao all invoked precedent to justify recall from mourning.

sentences.zh: 然天下壞亂，社稷傾危，流禍當時，遺譏後代。

translations.literal: Yet the realm fell into ruin and disorder, the altars of soil and grain were endangered, calamity flowed in that age, and reproach was left to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The realm then fell into chaos, the altars of state were endangered, disaster spread through the age, and posterity still heaps reproach upon their names.

sentences.zh: 無他，君不教臣以孝，臣無孝可移於君也。

translations.literal: There is nothing else to it: the ruler did not teach his ministers through filial piety, and the ministers had no filial piety that could be transferred to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is the same: the ruler did not teach his ministers through filial piety, and the ministers had no filial piety to offer up to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲賢身任天下之事，則賢身不可留，口實可言。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must have Xian personally undertake the affairs of the realm, then Xian's person cannot remain, yet grounds for criticism may be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes Li Xian to shoulder the affairs of the realm in person, then he cannot remain in mourning—but then there will be grounds for criticism that cannot be silenced.

sentences.zh: 宜降溫詔，俾如劉珙得以言事。

translations.literal: It is fitting to issue a gentle edict, enabling him as Liu Gong was enabled to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should issue a gracious edict, as with Liu Gong, allowing him to state his views fully.

sentences.zh: 使賢於天下之事知必言，言必盡。

translations.literal: Let Xian, regarding the affairs of the realm, know that he must speak and speak to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Let Li Xian know that on affairs of state he must speak, and speak without reserve.

sentences.zh: 陛下於賢之言聞必行，行必力。

translations.literal: Let Your Majesty, upon hearing Xian's words, act without fail and act with force.
translations.idiomatic: And let Your Majesty, when you hear his words, act on them without fail and act with full resolve.

sentences.zh: 賢雖不起復，猶起復也。

translations.literal: Though Xian is not recalled from mourning, it is still as if he were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Li Xian is not recalled from mourning, it will be as though he had been.

sentences.zh: 茍知之而不能盡言，言之而不能力行，賢雖起復無益也。

translations.literal: If he knows yet cannot speak fully, or speaks yet cannot act with force, then though Xian is recalled it is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: But if he knows yet cannot speak fully, or speaks yet Your Majesty cannot act with resolve, then recalling Li Xian will do no good at all.

sentences.zh: 且陛下無謂廟堂無賢臣，庶官無賢士。

translations.literal: Moreover, let Your Majesty not say that in the hall of state there are no worthy ministers, or among the multitude of offices no worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty should not suppose that the court lacks worthy ministers or that the ranks of officials lack worthy men.

sentences.zh: 君，盂也；

translations.literal: The ruler is the basin;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is like a basin;

sentences.zh: 臣，水也。

translations.literal: the ministers are the water.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers are like water.

sentences.zh: 水之方圓，盂實主之。

translations.literal: Whether the water is square or round, the basin in fact governs it.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the water takes a square or round shape, it is the basin that determines it.

sentences.zh: 臣之直佞，君實召之。

translations.literal: Whether ministers are upright or fawning, the ruler in fact summons it.
translations.idiomatic: Whether ministers are upright or fawning, it is the ruler who summons that quality forth.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠於退朝之暇，親直諒博洽之臣，講聖學君德之要，詢政事得失，察民生利病，訪人才賢否，考古今盛衰。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly, in the leisure after retiring from court, personally draws near upright, sincere, and broadly learned ministers, discusses the essentials of sagely learning and rulerly virtue, inquires into the gains and losses of government affairs, examines the benefits and harms to the people's livelihood, visits into whether talents are worthy or not, and investigates the flourishing and decline of past and present
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty, in the hours after court, would truly draw near upright, candid, and broadly learned ministers, discuss the essentials of sagely learning and rulerly virtue, inquire into what is right and wrong in government, examine the welfare and hardships of the people, seek out whether men of talent are worthy or not, and study the rise and fall of past and present ages

sentences.zh: 舍獨信之偏見，納逆耳之苦言。

translations.literal: abandon partial views in which one trusts only oneself, and accept bitter words that offend the ear,
translations.idiomatic: set aside partial views and private convictions, and accept blunt counsel that offends the ear,

sentences.zh: 則眾賢群策畢萃於朝，又何待違先王之《禮經》，損大臣之名節，然後天下可治哉。

translations.literal: then the worthy will all gather and strategies will assemble at court—why must one wait to violate the former kings' Classic of Rites, injure a great minister's name and integrity, and only then bring the realm to order?
translations.idiomatic: then every worthy man and every sound policy will gather at court. Why must Your Majesty violate the former kings' Classic of Rites and damage a great minister's reputation before the realm can be governed?

sentences.zh: 臣伏見比年以來，朝廷以奪情為常典，縉紳以起復為美名，食稻衣錦之徒，接踵廟堂，不知此人於天下之重何關耶？

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that in recent years the court has made curtailing mourning the regular rule, and gentry and officials have made recall from mourning a fine reputation; those who eat rice and wear brocade follow one upon another into the hall of state—does Your Majesty not know what relation such men bear to the weight of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has observed that in recent years the court has treated curtailing mourning as routine, and officials have treated recall from mourning as a mark of honor. Men who still feast on rice and dress in brocade stream one after another into the halls of government—what do such men have to do with the weighty affairs of the realm?

sentences.zh: 且婦於舅姑，喪亦三年；

translations.literal: Moreover, for a wife toward parents-in-law, mourning is also three years;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a wife mourns her parents-in-law for three years as well;

sentences.zh: 孫於祖父母，服則齊衰。

translations.literal: for a grandson toward grandparents, the garment is one year of qi mourning.
translations.idiomatic: a grandson wears one year of qi mourning for his grandparents.

sentences.zh: 奪情於夫，初無預其妻；

translations.literal: Curtailing mourning for the husband at first has nothing to do with his wife;
translations.idiomatic: When mourning is curtailed for a husband, it does not affect his wife;

sentences.zh: 奪情於父，初無幹其子。

translations.literal: curtailing mourning for the father at first does not involve his son.
translations.idiomatic: when mourning is curtailed for a father, it does not involve his son.

sentences.zh: 今或舍館如故，妻孥不還，乃號於天下曰：「本欲終喪，朝命不許」，雖三尺童子，臣知其不信也。

translations.literal: Now some keep their lodges as before and do not bring wife and children back, yet cry to the realm: "I originally wished to complete mourning, but the court's command would not allow it"—even a three-foot child, your subject knows, would not believe this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now some keep their lodgings as before and do not bring wife and children home, yet proclaim to the world, "I wished to complete my mourning, but the court would not permit it"—even a child of three feet, your subject knows, would not believe them.

sentences.zh: 為人父者所以望其子之報，豈擬至於此哉。

translations.literal: What a father hopes for in his son's requital—could he ever expect it to come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Is this what any father could expect from the requital he hopes for from his son?

sentences.zh: 為人子者所以報其親之心，豈忍至於此哉。

translations.literal: What a son's heart in requiting his parents is—could he bear to come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Could any son's heart in repaying his parents bear to come to this?

sentences.zh: 枉己者不能直人，忘親者不能忠君。

translations.literal: One who bends himself cannot straighten others; one who forgets his parents cannot be loyal to his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: One who bends himself cannot set others straight; one who forgets his parents cannot be loyal to his ruler.

sentences.zh: 陛下何取於若人而起復之也。

translations.literal: What does Your Majesty find in such men that you recall them from mourning?
translations.idiomatic: What does Your Majesty see in such men that you would recall them from mourning?

sentences.zh: 今大臣起復，群臣不以為非，且從而贊之；

translations.literal: Now when great ministers are recalled from mourning, the multitude of officials do not regard it as wrong but even follow and praise it;
translations.idiomatic: Today, when great ministers are recalled from mourning, the officials do not regard it as wrong but even follow and praise it;

sentences.zh: 群臣起復，大臣不以為非，且從而成之。

translations.literal: when the multitude of officials are recalled, great ministers do not regard it as wrong but even follow and accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: when lesser officials are recalled, the great ministers do not regard it as wrong but even follow and enable it.

sentences.zh: 上下成俗，混然同流，率天下之人為無父之歸。

translations.literal: Above and below form custom, muddled in one current, leading all under Heaven to become men who have returned without fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below have made a custom of it, flowing together in one stream, leading all under Heaven to become men who act as though they had no fathers.

sentences.zh: 臣不忍聖明之朝致綱常之壞、風俗之弊一至此極也。

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear that in this sage and enlightened court the cardinal norms should be ruined and customs corrupted to such an extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cannot bear to see this sage and enlightened court allow the cardinal norms to collapse and customs to decay to such an extreme.

sentences.zh: 願陛下斷自聖衷，許賢歸家持服。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to decide from your sage heart and permit Xian to return home to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty, deciding from your own sage heart, will permit Li Xian to return home and complete his mourning.

sentences.zh: 其他已起復者，仍令奔喪，未起復者，悉許終制。

translations.literal: As for others already recalled, still order them to rush home for mourning; those not yet recalled, entirely permit them to complete the full observance.
translations.idiomatic: As for others already recalled, order them back to complete their mourning; as for those not yet recalled, permit them all to observe the full term.

sentences.zh: 脫有金革之變，亦從墨衰之權，使任軍事於外，盡心喪於內。

translations.literal: If there should be change of arms and armor, then follow also the expedient of ink mourning garments, letting them undertake military affairs outside while fulfilling mourning with full heart within.
translations.idiomatic: If there should be military emergency, then follow the expedient of shortened mourning dress, letting them command armies abroad while fulfilling mourning duties at home with full devotion.

sentences.zh: 將朝廷端則天下一，大臣法則群臣效，人倫由是明，風俗由是厚矣。

translations.literal: Then if the court is upright the realm will be one, if great ministers set the model the multitude of officials will follow, human relations will thereby be clarified, and customs will thereby be thickened.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with the court upright the realm will be united, with great ministers setting the model the officials will follow, human relations will be clarified, and customs will be strengthened.

sentences.zh: 疏入，謫福建市舶司副提舉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Fujian Maritime Trade Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Fujian Maritime Trade Office.

sentences.zh: 御史陳選疏救，不報。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Xuan submitted a memorial in his defense; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Xuan submitted a memorial in his defense, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 御史楊瑯復申救，帝切責之。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Lang again pleaded for his rescue; the emperor sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Lang again pleaded on his behalf; the emperor sharply rebuked Yang.

sentences.zh: 尚書王翺以文彥博救唐介事諷賢，賢曰：「潞公市恩，歸怨朝廷，吾不可以效之。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Ao, citing Wen Yanbo's rescue of Tang Jie, admonished Xian; Xian said: "The Duke of Lu curried favor and shifted blame to the court—I cannot imitate that."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Ao, alluding to how Wen Yanbo had rescued Tang Jie, urged Li Xian to intervene; Li replied, "The Duke of Lu traded favors and shifted blame onto the court—I cannot imitate that."

sentences.zh: 」亡何，賢卒。

translations.literal: " Before long, Xian died.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long, Li Xian died.

sentences.zh: 明年以學士商輅言召復原職，改南京。

translations.literal: The next year, on the word of Academician Shang Lu, he was summoned to his former post, transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on Academician Shang Lu's recommendation, he was recalled to his former post and transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 居二年，引疾歸，遂不復出。

translations.literal: After two years in residence, he cited illness and returned home, and thereafter did not come forth again.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he cited illness and retired home, and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 倫為人剛正，嚴於律己。

translations.literal: Lun as a man was sternly upright and strict in disciplining himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was sternly upright and rigorous in disciplining himself.

sentences.zh: 義所在，毅然必為，於富貴名利泊如也。

translations.literal: Where righteousness lay, he resolutely must act; toward wealth, honor, fame, and profit he was indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Where righteousness required action, he acted resolutely; toward wealth, rank, fame, and profit he was utterly indifferent.

sentences.zh: 裏居倡行鄉約，相率無敢犯。

translations.literal: Living in his village he advocated the village covenant; leading one another, none dared violate it.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he promoted the village covenant, and the community followed him so faithfully that none dared violate it.

sentences.zh: 衣食粗惡。

translations.literal: His food and clothing were coarse and poor.
translations.idiomatic: His food and clothing were coarse and plain.

sentences.zh: 或遺之衣，見道堇，解以覆之。

translations.literal: When someone gave him clothing, if he saw purslane on the road he would undo it to cover the plant.
translations.idiomatic: When someone gave him clothing and he saw purslane growing by the roadside, he would take off the garment to cover the plants.

sentences.zh: 晨留客飲，妻子貸粟鄰家，及午方炊，不為意。

translations.literal: One morning he kept a guest to drink; his wife borrowed grain from a neighbor, and only at noon did they cook—he paid it no mind.
translations.idiomatic: One morning he kept a guest for wine; his wife had to borrow grain from a neighbor, and they did not cook until noon—he thought nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 以金牛山人跡不至，築室著書其中，四方從學者甚眾。

translations.literal: Because on Mount Jinniu human tracks did not come, he built a chamber and wrote books therein; learners from the four quarters were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mount Jinniu was secluded and rarely visited, he built a study there and wrote books; students came from all directions in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Chenghua, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，從御史唐龍請，追贈左春坊諭德，謚文毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, following Censor Tang Long's request, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Sub-Reader of the Eastern Palace and given the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, on Censor Tang Long's petition, he was posthumously appointed Left Sub-Reader of the Eastern Palace and given the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 學者稱一峰先生。

translations.literal: Scholars call him Master Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honor him as Master Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 方倫為提舉時，御史豐城塗棐巡按福建。

translations.literal: When Lun was commissioner, Censor Tu Fei of Fengcheng was touring and inspecting Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: While Lun was serving as commissioner, Censor Tu Fei of Fengcheng was conducting an inspection tour of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 司禮中官黃賜，延平人也，請見，棐不可。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Huang Ci, a native of Yanping, requested an audience; Fei would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ci, a eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial and a native of Yanping, asked for an audience; Tu Fei refused.

sentences.zh: 泉州知府李宗學以受賕為棐所按，訐棐自解，賜從中主其奏。

translations.literal: Quanzhou Prefect Li Zongxue, because he had accepted bribes, was impeached by Fei; he denounced Fei to clear himself, and Ci from within backed his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongxue, prefect of Quanzhou, was impeached by Tu Fei for taking bribes; Li counter-attacked Tu Fei to clear himself, and Huang Ci intervened from within the palace to support Li's memorial.

sentences.zh: 棐、宗學俱被征，詞連倫，當並逮。

translations.literal: Fei and Zongxue were both summoned; their words implicated Lun, and he ought to have been arrested together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Both Tu Fei and Li Zongxue were summoned to the capital; their testimony implicated Lun, and he too was due to be arrested.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司某曰：「羅先生可至此乎？

translations.literal: A certain man of the Brocade Guard said: "Could Master Luo come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone in the Brocade Guard said, "Could Master Luo really have come to this?"

sentences.zh: 」即日鞫成上之。

translations.literal: " That same day the case was tried, concluded, and submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day the case was tried, concluded, and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 倫得免，棐亦復官。

translations.literal: Lun was spared; Fei also regained his office.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was spared, and Tu Fei was also restored to office.

sentences.zh: 塗棐，天順四年進士。

translations.literal: Tu Fei was a jinshi of the fourth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Fei passed the jinshi examination in 1460.

sentences.zh: 成化中嘗言：「祖宗朝，政事必與大臣面議。

translations.literal: During Chenghua he once said: "In the reigns of the ancestral emperors, government affairs had to be discussed face to face with great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he once said, "Under the founding emperors, state affairs were always discussed face to face with the senior ministers."

sentences.zh: 自先帝幼沖，未能裁決，柄國者慮其缺遺，假簡易之辭，以便宣布。

translations.literal: Since the former emperor was young and in his minority and could not decide, those who held the realm feared omissions, and used simple, easy words to facilitate promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: After the former emperor came to the throne as a child and could not decide matters himself, those who held power, fearing omissions, used brief formulas to make announcements easier.

sentences.zh: 凡視朝奏事，諭旨輒曰：「所司知之」。

translations.literal: Whenever one attended court and reported affairs, the edict of instruction would always say: "Let the relevant office know."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officials reported business at court, the imperial response would simply say, "Let the relevant office handle it."

sentences.zh: 此一時權宜，非可循為定制。

translations.literal: This was a temporary expedient of the moment, not something that can be followed as a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: This was a temporary expedient, not a practice that should become permanent custom.

sentences.zh: 況批答多參以中官，內閣或不與，尤乖祖制。

translations.literal: Moreover, many rescripts were drafted with eunuchs participating; the Grand Secretariat sometimes was not involved—this especially departed from ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many rescripts were drafted with eunuchs involved, and the Grand Secretariat was sometimes left out—this departed especially far from ancestral practice.

sentences.zh: 乞復面議，杜蔽壅之弊。

translations.literal: I beg to restore face-to-face discussion and stop up the abuses of concealment and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that face-to-face deliberation be restored, to cut off the abuses of concealment and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 」憲宗不能用。

translations.literal: " The Xianzong Emperor could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Xianzong Emperor did not adopt his proposal.

sentences.zh: 終廣東副使。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 章懋，字德懋，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao, styled Demao, was a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao, styled Demao, was from Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 成化二年會試第一，成進士，改庶吉王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he placed first in the metropolitan examination, became a jinshi, and was made a Metropolitan Graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1466 he placed first in the metropolitan examination, became a jinshi, and entered the Hanlin as a Metropolitan Graduate.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，授編修。

translations.literal: The next winter he was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 憲宗將以元夕張燈，命詞臣撰詩詞進奉。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor was about to hang lanterns for the Lantern Festival and ordered literary officials to compose poems and lyrics to present.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianzong Emperor planned to display lanterns for the Lantern Festival and ordered the literary officials to compose poems and lyrics for presentation.

sentences.zh: 懋與同官黃仲昭、檢討莊昶疏諫曰：「頃諭臣等撰鰲山煙火詩詞，臣等竊議，此必非陛下本懷，或以兩宮聖母在上，欲備極孝養奉其歡心耳。

translations.literal: Mao, together with his colleague Huang Zhongzhao and Reviser Zhuang Chang, submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "Recently Your Majesty instructed us to compose poems and lyrics for the Ao Mountain fireworks; we privately discussed this and thought it surely cannot be Your Majesty's original intent, or perhaps because the two palaces' sage mothers are above, you wish to prepare the utmost filial nurture to please their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Mao, together with his colleague Huang Zhongzhao and Reviser Zhuang Chang, submitted a remonstrance that read: "Your Majesty recently instructed us to compose poems and lyrics for the Ao Mountain fireworks display. We discussed this privately and believe this cannot be Your Majesty's true intent—or perhaps, with the empress dowagers above, you wish to offer the utmost filial display to please them."

sentences.zh: 然大孝在乎養誌，不可徒陳耳目之玩以為養也。

translations.literal: Yet great filial piety lies in nurturing the parents' will; one cannot merely set forth playthings for the ears and eyes and call it nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Yet true filial piety lies in honoring one's parents' wishes, not in offering mere spectacles for the senses and calling that nurture.

sentences.zh: 今川東未靖，遼左多虞，江西、湖廣赤地數千里，萬姓嗷嗷，張口待哺，此正陛下宵旰焦勞，兩宮母後同憂天下之日。

translations.literal: Now Sichuan east is not yet pacified, Liaodong left has many alarms, Jiangxi and Huguang have bare earth for thousands of li, and the myriad people cry out, opening their mouths awaiting nourishment—this is precisely the day when Your Majesty should toil from dusk till dawn in anxiety, and the two palaces' empresses should share worry for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Sichuan is not yet pacified, Liaodong faces many threats, and in Jiangxi and Huguang bare earth stretches for thousands of li while the people cry out for food. This is precisely the time when Your Majesty should labor anxiously from dawn to dusk, and when the empress dowagers should share the realm's troubles.

sentences.zh: 至翰林官以論思為職，鄙俚之言豈宜進於君上。

translations.literal: As for Hanlin officials, their duty is deliberation and reflection—how can vulgar words be fitting to present to the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin officials are charged with deliberation and counsel—how can vulgar words be presented to the throne?

sentences.zh: 伏讀宣宗皇帝御制《翰林箴》有曰『啟沃之言，唯義與仁。

translations.literal: Your subjects have read the Xuanzong Emperor's imperial composition "Admonition for the Hanlin," which says: "Words of counsel and nourishment—only righteousness and benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: We have read the Xuanzong Emperor's imperial composition Admonition for the Hanlin, which says, "Words of counsel should speak only of righteousness and benevolence."

sentences.zh: 堯、舜之道，鄒、魯以陳。

translations.literal: The way of Yao and Shun—Zou and Lu are the ones to set it forth."
translations.idiomatic: The way of Yao and Shun should be set forth in the manner of the sages of Zou and Lu."

sentences.zh: 』張燈豈堯、舜之道，詩詞豈仁義之言？

translations.literal: " Is hanging lanterns the way of Yao and Shun? Are poems and lyrics words of benevolence and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: " Are hanging lanterns the way of Yao and Shun? Are festive poems and lyrics words of benevolence and righteousness?

sentences.zh: 若謂煙火細故不足為聖德累，則舜何必不造漆器，禹何必不嗜旨酒，漢文何必不作露臺？

translations.literal: If one says fireworks are a small matter and cannot burden sagely virtue, then why did Shun not make lacquer vessels, why did Yu not love fine wine, why did Emperor Wen of Han not build the Terrace of Dew?
translations.idiomatic: If one says fireworks are trifles that cannot burden sagely virtue, then why did Shun refrain from making lacquer vessels, why did Yu refrain from fine wine, and why did Emperor Wen of Han refrain from building the Terrace of Dew?

sentences.zh: 古帝王慎小謹微必矜細行者，正以欲不可縱，漸不可長也。

translations.literal: Ancient emperors and kings were cautious in small matters, careful in minute things, and necessarily strict in fine conduct—precisely because desire must not be indulged and gradual growth must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient emperors were cautious in small matters and strict in minute conduct precisely because desire must not be indulged and small excesses must not be allowed to grow.

sentences.zh: 伏乞將煙火停止，移此視聽以明目達聰，省此資財以振饑恤困，則災祲可銷，太平可致。

translations.literal: Your subjects beg that the fireworks be stopped, that this attention be shifted to brighten the eyes and sharpen the hearing, that these resources be saved to relieve famine and succor distress—then calamity and ill omen can be dispelled and great peace can be attained.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that the fireworks be stopped, that this attention be turned to clear sight and keen hearing in governance, and that these resources be saved to relieve famine and succor the distressed—then calamities can be dispelled and great peace attained.

sentences.zh: 」帝以元夕張燈，祖宗故事，惡懋等妄言，並杖之闕下，左遷其官。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because hanging lanterns on the Lantern Festival was ancestral precedent, hated Mao and the others for reckless speech, had them all beaten below the palace gate, and demoted their offices.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, holding that Lantern Festival displays were ancestral precedent, resented their reckless remonstrance, had them all beaten below the palace gate, and demoted them.

sentences.zh: 修撰羅倫先以言事被黜，時稱「翰林四諫」。

translations.literal: Academician Editor Luo Lun had earlier been dismissed for speaking on affairs; at the time they were called "the Four Remonstrators of the Hanlin."
translations.idiomatic: Academician Editor Luo Lun had already been dismissed for remonstrating on policy; together they were known as "the Four Remonstrators of the Hanlin."

sentences.zh: 懋既貶臨武知縣，未行，以給事中毛弘等論救，改南京大理左評事。

translations.literal: After Mao was demoted to magistrate of Linwu, before he departed, on the discussion and rescue of Supervising Secretary Mao Hong and others, he was changed to Left Assessor of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was demoted to magistrate of Linwu, but before he departed, Supervising Secretary Mao Hong and others pleaded on his behalf, and he was reassigned as Left Assessor of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，遷福建僉事。

translations.literal: After more than three years he was transferred to Fujian as Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was transferred to Fujian as Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 平泰寧、沙、尤賊，聽福安民采礦以杜盜源，建議番貨互通貿易以裕商民，政績甚著。

translations.literal: He pacified the bandits of Taining, Sha, and You, permitted the people of Fu'an to mine ore to cut off the source of banditry, and proposed that foreign goods exchange in trade to enrich merchants and people—his administrative achievements were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified bandits in Taining, Sha, and You, allowed the people of Fu'an to mine ore to cut off the source of banditry, and proposed mutual trade in foreign goods to enrich merchants and commoners—his administrative record was outstanding.

sentences.zh: 滿考入都，年止四十一，力求致仕。

translations.literal: When his term was complete and he entered the capital for evaluation, he was only forty-one and strongly sought to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to the capital for evaluation, he was only forty-one and urgently sought retirement.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書尹旻固留之，不可。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yin Min firmly kept him, but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yin Min pressed him to stay, but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 既歸，屏跡不入城府。

translations.literal: After returning, he hid his tracks and did not enter prefectural or district cities.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he kept out of public offices and never entered the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 奉親之暇，專以讀書講學為事，弟子執經者日益進。

translations.literal: In the leisure of serving his parents, he devoted himself solely to reading books and lecturing on learning; disciples who held the classics daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of caring for his parents, he devoted himself to reading and teaching; the number of students who came to study the classics with him grew daily.

sentences.zh: 貧無供具，惟脫粟菜羹而已。

translations.literal: Poor, he had no provisions for guests—only husked grain and vegetable broth.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to offer guests fine fare, he had only plain grain and vegetable broth.

sentences.zh: 四方學士大夫高其風，稱為「楓山先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials from the four quarters esteemed his conduct and called him "Master Fengshan."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars throughout the realm admired his conduct and called him Master Fengshan.

sentences.zh: 家居二十余年，中外交薦，部檄屢起之，以親老堅不赴。

translations.literal: Living at home for more than twenty years, within and without the court he was recommended; the ministry repeatedly issued orders summoning him, but because his parents were old he firmly would not go.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than twenty years. Recommendations poured in from court and countryside, and the ministry repeatedly summoned him, but while his parents lived he steadfastly refused to return to office.

sentences.zh: 懋為學，恪守先儒訓。

translations.literal: In learning, Mao strictly kept the teachings of former Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship Mao strictly adhered to the teachings of the earlier Confucians.

sentences.zh: 或諷為文章，曰：「小技耳，予弗暇。

translations.literal: When someone urged him to write literary compositions, he said: "A petty skill—I have no leisure."
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to write literary compositions, he replied, "That is a petty skill—I have no time for it."

sentences.zh: 」有勸以著述者，曰：「先儒之言至矣，芟其繁可也。

translations.literal: " When someone urged him to compose books, he said: "The words of former Confucians are already complete—one need only prune what is redundant."
translations.idiomatic: " When someone urged him to write books, he said, "The earlier Confucians have already said everything—one need only prune what is redundant."

sentences.zh: 」通籍五十余年，歷俸僅滿三考。

translations.literal: " Having entered the registers for more than fifty years, the salaries he received barely filled three evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: " Though he had been on the official rolls for more than fifty years, the salary he actually drew barely covered three evaluation cycles.

sentences.zh: 難進易退，世皆高之。

translations.literal: Hard to advance, easy to withdraw—the world all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctant to advance yet quick to withdraw, he was universally admired.

sentences.zh: 生三子，兼令業農。

translations.literal: He had three sons and also made them practice farming.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons and made them farm as well.

sentences.zh: 縣令過之，諸子釋耒跪迎，人不知其貴公子也。

translations.literal: When the district magistrate passed by, his sons put down their hoes and knelt to welcome him; people did not know they were the sons of a noble gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the district magistrate visited, his sons would set down their hoes and kneel to receive him—no one would have guessed they were the sons of a distinguished official.

sentences.zh: 子省懋於南監，徒步往，道為巡檢所笞，已知而請罪，懋慰遣之。

translations.literal: A son visited Mao at the Southern Directorate; he went on foot and on the road was beaten by a patrol inspector. After he was known and asked forgiveness, Mao comforted and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: One son visited Mao at the Southern Directorate on foot; along the way a patrol inspector beat him. Once the inspector learned who he was and apologized, Mao comforted him and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 晚年，三子一孫盡死。

translations.literal: In his later years his three sons and one grandson all died.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years all three sons and one grandson died.

sentences.zh: 年八十二生少子接，後以蔭為國子生。

translations.literal: At age eighty-two he bore a younger son Jie, who later through yin privilege became a student of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-two he fathered a younger son named Jie, who later entered the Directorate of Education by yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 從子拯，字以道。

translations.literal: His nephew Zheng, styled Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zheng, styled Yidao.

sentences.zh: 幼從懋學，登弘治十五年進士，為刑部主事。

translations.literal: From youth he studied under Mao, passed as jinshi in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, and became a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Mao from childhood, passed the jinshi examination in 1502, and became a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 正德初，忤劉瑾，下詔獄，謫梧州府通判。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he offended Liu Jin, was sent to the imperial prison, and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he offended Liu Jin, was imprisoned, and was demoted to vice prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 謹誅，擢南京兵部郎中。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he was promoted to director in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，累官工部尚書。

translations.literal: During Jiajing he rose through offices to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he rose through successive posts to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 桂萼欲復海運，延公卿議得失，拯曰：「海運雖有故事，而風濤百倍於河。

translations.literal: Gui E wished to restore sea transport; he summoned dukes and ministers to discuss gains and losses. Zheng said: "Though sea transport has precedent, wind and waves are a hundred times those of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Gui E wished to restore sea transport and summoned the senior officials to debate the matter. Zheng said, "Sea transport has precedent, but wind and waves on the open sea are a hundred times worse than on the rivers."

sentences.zh: 且天津海口多淤，自古不聞有浚海者。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Tianjin sea mouth is much silted; from antiquity one has never heard of dredging the sea."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the mouth of the sea at Tianjin is heavily silted, and since antiquity no one has ever heard of dredging the open sea."

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢。

translations.literal: " The discussion was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 南北郊議起，拯言不可，失帝意。

translations.literal: When discussion of separate southern and northern suburban sacrifices arose, Zheng said it could not be done and lost the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the debate over separate southern and northern suburban sacrifices arose, Zheng opposed it and lost the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 尋坐郊壇祭器缺供，落職歸。

translations.literal: Soon, on the charge that sacrificial vessels for the suburban altars were lacking in supply, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was dismissed and sent home on the charge that sacrificial vessels for the suburban altars had not been supplied.

sentences.zh: 久之復官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died.

sentences.zh: 黃仲昭，名潛，以字行，莆田人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhongzhao, personal name Qian, known by his style, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhongzhao, personal name Qian, known by his style, was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 祖壽生，翰林檢討，有學行。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shousheng was a Hanlin Reviser and had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shousheng had been a Hanlin Reviser and was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 父嘉，束鹿知縣，以善政聞。

translations.literal: His father Jia was magistrate of Shulu and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jia had been magistrate of Shulu and was known for good governance.

sentences.zh: 仲昭性端謹，年十五六即有誌正學。

translations.literal: Zhongzhao by nature was proper and cautious; at fifteen or sixteen he already had the will for correct learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhao was by nature proper and cautious; by fifteen or sixteen he was already resolved to pursue true learning.

sentences.zh: 登成化二年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the second year of Chenghua, was made a Metropolitan Graduate, and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1466, entered the Hanlin as a Metropolitan Graduate, and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 與章懋、莊同以直諫被杖，謫湘潭知縣。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Mao and Zhuang Chang he was beaten for direct remonstrance and demoted to magistrate of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang Mao and Zhuang Chang he was beaten for blunt remonstrance and demoted to magistrate of Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 在道，用諫官言，改南京大理評事。

translations.literal: On the road, on the word of remonstrance officials, he was changed to Assessor of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: While still on the road to his post, on the recommendation of remonstrance officials he was reassigned as assessor of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 兩京諸司隸卒率放還而取其月錢，為故事，惟仲昭與羅倫不敢。

translations.literal: Runners attached to offices in the two capitals generally released them to return home while taking their monthly pay as established practice—only Zhongzhao and Luo Lun dared not.
translations.idiomatic: Runners attached to offices in both capitals were routinely sent home while their monthly pay was still collected—a standing abuse that only Zhongzhao and Luo Lun refused to follow.

sentences.zh: 御史縱子弟取賂，刑部曲為地，仲昭駁正之。

translations.literal: A censor indulged his sons and younger brothers in taking bribes; the Ministry of Justice bent the ground for them—Zhongzhao refuted and corrected this.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor allowed his sons to take bribes and the Ministry of Justice bent the law in their favor, Zhongzhao overturned the ruling.

sentences.zh: 有群掠民婦轉鬻者，部坐首惡一人，仲昭請皆坐。

translations.literal: There was a band that plundered commoners' wives and resold them; the ministry sentenced only the chief culprit—Zhongzhao requested that all be sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: When a gang abducted commoners' wives and resold them, the ministry convicted only the ringleader; Zhongzhao insisted that all be punished.

sentences.zh: 連遭父母喪，不離苫塊者四年。

translations.literal: He suffered successive mourning for his parents and did not leave the mourning hut for four years.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned both parents in succession and did not leave the mourning hut for four years.

sentences.zh: 服除，以親不逮養，遂不出。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, because his parents had not been able to enjoy his nurture, he therefore did not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, feeling that he had failed to nurture his parents while they lived, he never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，御史姜洪疏薦，吏部尚書王恕檄有司敦趣。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title in Hongzhi, Censor Jiang Hong memorialized to recommend him; Minister of Personnel Wang Su issued orders to local officials to urge him earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, Censor Jiang Hong recommended him in a memorial, and Minister of Personnel Wang Su ordered local officials to urge him to return.

sentences.zh: 比至，恕迓之大門外，揖讓升堂，相向再拜，世兩高之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Su met him outside the great gate; they bowed and yielded in ascending the hall, faced each other and bowed twice—the age esteemed both.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Wang Su met him outside the main gate; they bowed and yielded precedence as they entered the hall, then faced each other and bowed again—the age admired them both.

sentences.zh: 除江西提學僉事，誨士以正學。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Commissioner for Education in Jiangxi and instructed scholars in correct learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Commissioner for Education in Jiangxi and instructed scholars in orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 久之再疏乞休，日事著述。

translations.literal: After a long time he again memorialized begging to retire and daily devoted himself to writing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he again petitioned to retire and devoted himself daily to writing.

sentences.zh: 學者稱「未軒先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars call him "Master Weixuan."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honor him as Master Weixuan.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 仲昭兄深，御史。

translations.literal: Zhongzhao's elder brother Shen was a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhao's elder brother Shen was a censor.

sentences.zh: 深子乾亨，行人。

translations.literal: Shen's son Qianheng was a courier.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's son Qianheng was a courier.

sentences.zh: 使滿剌加，歿於海。

translations.literal: On a mission to Malacca, he died at sea.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Malacca he died at sea.

sentences.zh: 乾亨子如金，廣西提學副使，希雍，蘇州同知。

translations.literal: Qianheng's son Rujin was Vice Commissioner for Education in Guangxi; Xiyong was Vice Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qianheng's son Rujin became Vice Commissioner for Education in Guangxi; another descendant, Xiyong, became vice prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲昭孫懋，南京戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhongzhao's grandson Mao was Vice Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhao's grandson Mao became Vice Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 莊，字孔抃，江浦人。

translations.literal: Zhuang Chang, styled Kongbian, was a native of Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Chang, styled Kongbian, was from Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 自幼豪邁不群，嗜古博學。

translations.literal: From youth he was bold and ungrouped, loving antiquity and broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was bold and unconventional, devoted to antiquity and broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 舉成化二年進士，改庶吉士，授翰林檢討。

translations.literal: He was presented as jinshi in the second year of Chenghua, made a Metropolitan Graduate, and appointed Hanlin Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1466, entered the Hanlin as a Metropolitan Graduate, and was appointed Hanlin Reviser.

sentences.zh: 與編修章懋、黃仲昭疏諫內廷張燈，忤旨廷杖二十，謫桂陽州判官。

translations.literal: Together with Compiler Zhang Mao and Huang Zhongzhao he memorialized to remonstrate against hanging lanterns in the inner court; offending the decree he was beaten twenty times at court and demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Guiyang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Compiler Zhang Mao and Huang Zhongzhao he remonstrated against the inner court's Lantern Festival display; for offending the throne he was beaten twenty times at court and demoted to assistant magistrate of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 尋以言官論救，改南京行人司副。

translations.literal: Soon, on the discussion and rescue of remonstrance officials, he was changed to Vice Director of the Nanjing Courier Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on the plea of remonstrance officials, he was reassigned as vice director of the Nanjing Courier Office.

sentences.zh: 居三年，母憂去。

translations.literal: After three years in office he left on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he left to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 繼丁父憂，哀毀，喪除不復出。

translations.literal: He then suffered mourning for his father, was devastated in grief, and when mourning ended did not come forth again.
translations.idiomatic: He then mourned his father, was devastated by grief, and when mourning ended never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 卜居定山二十余年，學者稱「定山先生」。

translations.literal: He chose residence on Mount Dingshan for more than twenty years; scholars call him "Master Dingshan."
translations.idiomatic: He settled on Mount Dingshan for more than twenty years; scholars honor him as Master Dingshan.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王恕嘗欲葺其廬，辭之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Su once wished to repair his cottage; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Su once offered to repair his cottage; he declined.

sentences.zh: 昶生平不尚著述，有自得，輒見之於詩。

translations.literal: Chang in his life did not esteem composing books; when he had personal attainment, he always expressed it in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Chang did not value book-writing in his lifetime; when he had an insight, he expressed it in poetry.

sentences.zh: 薦章十余上，部檄屢趣，俱不赴。

translations.literal: More than ten recommendation memorials went up; the ministry repeatedly issued orders urging him—all he did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten recommendation memorials were submitted, and the ministry repeatedly summoned him, but he never went.

sentences.zh: 大學士邱濬素惡昶，語人曰：「率天下士背朝廷者，昶也。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Qiu Jun had always hated Chang and said to people: "The one who leads all scholars under Heaven to turn their backs on the court is Chang."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Qiu Jun had long disliked Chang and said to others, "The man who leads scholars throughout the realm to turn their backs on the court is Chang."

sentences.zh: 」弘治七年有薦昶者，奉詔起用。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Hongzhi someone recommended Chang; he received an edict to be raised and employed.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1494 someone recommended Chang, and he received an edict summoning him to office.

sentences.zh: 昶念濬當國，不出且得罪，強起入都。

translations.literal: Chang thought that with Jun holding the state, if he did not come forth he would yet offend, and forced himself to rise and enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chang thought that with Qiu Jun in power, if he did not go he would give offense anyway, and reluctantly set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 大學士徐溥語郎中邵寶曰：「定山故翰林，復之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Pu said to Director Shao Bao: "Dingshan is a former Hanlin man—restore him."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xu Pu said to Director Shao Bao, "Dingshan is a former Hanlin man—restore him to that status."

sentences.zh: 」濬聞曰：「我不識所謂定山也。

translations.literal: " Jun heard and said: "I do not know this so-called Dingshan."
translations.idiomatic: " When Qiu Jun heard this, he said, "I do not know any such person as Dingshan."

sentences.zh: 」乃復以為行人司副。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was again made Vice Director of the Courier Office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then reappointed as vice director of the Courier Office.

sentences.zh: 俄遷南京吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 得風疾。

translations.literal: He contracted wind illness.
translations.idiomatic: He contracted a paralytic disorder.

sentences.zh: 明年乞身歸，部臣不為奏。

translations.literal: The next year he begged to return home on his person; the ministry officials did not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he petitioned to retire, but the ministry officials did not forward his request.

sentences.zh: 又明年京祭，尚書倪嶽以老疾罷之。

translations.literal: The year after, at the capital sacrifices, Minister Ni Yue dismissed him on grounds of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, at the capital sacrifices, Minister Ni Yue dismissed him on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 居二年卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: After two years in residence he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚文節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously given the title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 鄒智，字汝愚，合州人。

translations.literal: Zou Zhi, styled Ruyu, was a native of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhi, styled Ruyu, was from Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 年十二能文。

translations.literal: At age twelve he could write compositions.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 家貧，讀書焚木葉繼晷者三年。

translations.literal: His family was poor; for three years he read by burning tree leaves to extend the daylight.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and for three years he studied by burning tree leaves to extend the daylight.

sentences.zh: 舉成化二十二年鄉試第一。

translations.literal: He was presented first in the provincial examination of the twenty-second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the provincial examination of 1486.

sentences.zh: 時帝益倦於政，而萬安、劉吉、尹直居政府，智憤之。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor grew ever more weary of government, while Wan An, Liu Ji, and Yin Zhi held the government—Zhi was indignant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was growing ever more weary of governing, while Wan An, Liu Ji, and Yin Zhi held power in the government; Zhi was deeply angered.

sentences.zh: 道出三原，謁致仕尚書王恕，慨然曰：「治天下，在進君子退小人。

translations.literal: Passing through Sanyuan, he visited retired Minister Wang Su and said with emotion: "To govern the realm lies in advancing gentlemen and retiring petty men."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Sanyuan, he visited the retired minister Wang Su and said with feeling, "To govern the realm is to advance gentlemen and dismiss petty men."

sentences.zh: 方今小人在位，毒痡四海，而公顧屏棄田裏。

translations.literal: Now petty men are in office, poisoning and ulcerating the four seas, yet you turn aside and abandon the fields and villages.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men now hold office and poison the realm, yet you withdraw to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 智此行非為科名，欲上書天子，別白賢奸，拯斯民於塗炭耳。

translations.literal: This journey of Zhi's is not for examination fame; I wish to submit a book to the Son of Heaven, distinguish the worthy from the treacherous, and rescue this people from charcoal and mud.
translations.idiomatic: I have not come for examination honors. I mean to submit a memorial to the Son of Heaven, distinguish the worthy from the wicked, and rescue the people from misery."

sentences.zh: 」恕奇其言，笑而不答。

translations.literal: " Su marveled at his words, smiled, and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Su marveled at his words, smiled, and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 明年登進士。

translations.literal: The next year he passed as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was made a Metropolitan Graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a Metropolitan Graduate.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 陛下於輔臣，遇事必咨，殊恩異數必及，亦雲任矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty toward assisting ministers, whenever affairs arise you must consult them, special favor and extraordinary treatment always reach them—this also may be called entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty consults your assisting ministers on every matter and bestows special favor upon them—this may be called entrustment indeed.

sentences.zh: 然或進退一人，處分一事，往往降中旨，使一二小人陰執其柄，是既任之而又疑之也。

translations.literal: Yet whether advancing or retiring a man, or disposing of an affair, you often issue inner edicts, letting one or two petty men secretly hold the handle—this is both entrusting them and yet doubting them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether promoting or dismissing a man, or deciding an affair, you often issue secret edicts, letting one or two petty men secretly hold real power—entrusting them and yet doubting them at once.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈不欲推誠待物哉？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty not wish to extend sincerity in treating things?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty not wish to treat your ministers with full sincerity?

sentences.zh: 由其進身之初，多出私門，先有以致陛下之厭薄。

translations.literal: Because at the beginning of their advancement they mostly came from private gates, this first gave cause for Your Majesty's disdain and contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Because they rose mostly through private connections, Your Majesty came to despise them from the start.

sentences.zh: 及與議事，又唯諾惟謹，伈々伣々，若有所不敢，反不如一二俗吏足以任事。

translations.literal: When they discuss affairs they only assent with caution, cringing and shrinking as if they dare not speak, and are not even equal to one or two vulgar clerks sufficient to undertake business.
translations.idiomatic: When they discuss affairs they only nod assent with exaggerated caution, cringing as if afraid to speak, and prove less useful than a common clerk.

sentences.zh: 此陛下所為疑也，臣竊以為過矣。

translations.literal: This is what Your Majesty doubts; your subject ventures to think it is a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Your Majesty doubts—but I venture to think the mistake lies elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 昔宋仁宗知夏竦懷詐則黜之，知呂夷簡能改過則容之；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Renzong of Song, knowing Xia Song harbored deceit, dismissed him; knowing Lü Yijian could reform his faults, tolerated him;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Renzong of Song, knowing that Xia Song harbored deceit, dismissed him; knowing that Lü Yijian could reform his faults, tolerated him;

sentences.zh: 知杜衍、韓琦、範仲淹、富弼可任則不次擢之。

translations.literal: knowing Du Yan, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi could be entrusted, promoted them out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: knowing that Du Yan, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi were fit for office, promoted them out of turn.

sentences.zh: 故能北拒契丹，西臣元昊。

translations.literal: Therefore he could resist the Khitan in the north and make Yuan Hao submit in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was able to hold the Khitan in the north and subdue Yuan Hao in the west.

sentences.zh: 未聞一任一疑，可以成天下事也。

translations.literal: One has never heard that entrusting yet doubting can accomplish the affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: No one has ever heard that entrusting and doubting at once can accomplish the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察孰為竦，孰為夷簡，而黜之容之，孰為衍、琦、仲淹、弼而擢之，日與講論治道，不使小人得參其間，則天工亮矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to discern who is Song and who is Yijian, and dismiss or tolerate them; who are Yan, Qi, Zhongyan, and Bi, and promote them; daily discuss the way of governing with them and do not let petty men participate among them—then the heavenly work will be bright.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty discern who are like Song and who like Yijian, and dismiss or tolerate them accordingly; discern who are like Yan, Qi, Zhongyan, and Bi, and promote them; discuss the way of governing with them daily and keep petty men from intervening—then Heaven's work will be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞天下事惟輔臣得議，惟諫官得言。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that affairs of the realm may be discussed only by assisting ministers, and spoken of only by remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that affairs of the realm may be deliberated only by assisting ministers and spoken of only by remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 諫官雖卑，與輔臣等。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials, though low in rank, are equal to assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials, though low in rank, stand equal to assisting ministers.

sentences.zh: 乃今之諫官以軀體魁梧為美，以應對捷給為賢，以簿書刑獄為職業。

translations.literal: Yet today's remonstrance officials take a tall, sturdy body as beauty, quick and ready response as worth, and documents and criminal cases as their profession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today's remonstrance officials prize tall stature, quick repartee, and treat paperwork and criminal cases as their profession.

sentences.zh: 不畏天變，不恤人窮。

translations.literal: They do not fear heavenly changes and do not pity human destitution.
translations.idiomatic: They do not fear heavenly warnings and do not pity the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 或以忠義激之，則曰：「吾非不欲言，言出則禍隨，其誰吾聽？

translations.literal: When stirred by loyalty and righteousness, they say: "It is not that I do not wish to speak; once words go forth calamity follows—who will heed me?"
translations.idiomatic: When stirred by loyalty and righteousness, they say, "It is not that I do not wish to speak—but once words go forth, calamity follows. Who will heed me?"

sentences.zh: 」嗚呼！

translations.literal: " Alas!
translations.idiomatic: " Alas!

sentences.zh: 既不能盡言效職，而復引過以歸於上。

translations.literal: Unable to speak fully and perform their duty, they yet shift blame upward to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to speak fully and perform their duty, they shift the blame upward onto the throne.

sentences.zh: 有人心者固如是乎？

translations.literal: Can those who have a human heart truly be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Can any man with a human heart truly act like this?

sentences.zh: 臣願罷黜浮冗，廣求風節之臣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to dismiss the floating and redundant and broadly seek ministers of moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes to dismiss the superfluous and seek broadly for men of moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 令仗下糾彈，入閣參議。

translations.literal: Let them impeach below the imperial staff and enter the Grand Secretariat to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Let them impeach wrongdoing at court and enter the Grand Secretariat to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 或請對，或輪對，或非時召對，霽色接之，溫言導之，使得畢誠盡蘊，則天聽開矣。

translations.literal: Whether requesting audience, rotating audience, or being summoned at irregular times, receive them with clear countenance and guide them with warm words, enabling them to exhaust sincerity and fully express their thoughts—then Heaven's hearing will be open.
translations.idiomatic: Whether by requested audience, rotating audience, or irregular summons, receive them with an open countenance and guide them with warm words, so that they may speak with full sincerity—then Heaven's ear will be open.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞汲黯在朝，淮南寢謀，君子之有益人國也大矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that when Ji An was at court, Huainan's plots lay dormant—the benefit of gentlemen to the people's state is indeed great.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that while Ji An was at court, Huainan's plots lay dormant—the benefit gentlemen bring to the state is indeed great.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之聰明，寧不知君子可任而故屈抑之哉？

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's intelligence, would you not know that gentlemen can be entrusted yet deliberately suppress them?
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's intelligence, would you not know that gentlemen can be entrusted—yet deliberately hold them down?

sentences.zh: 乃小人巧讒間以中傷之耳。

translations.literal: It is only that petty men by crafty slander and alienation wound them.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that petty men wound them through crafty slander.

sentences.zh: 今碩德如王恕，忠鯁如強珍，亮直剛方如章懋、林俊、張吉，皆一時人望，不宜貶錮，負上天生才之意。

translations.literal: Now great virtue such as Wang Su, loyal bluntness such as Qiang Zhen, bright uprightness and stern integrity such as Zhang Mao, Lin Jun, and Zhang Ji—all are the people's hope of the age and should not be demoted and confined, betraying Heaven's intent in producing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Men of great virtue such as Wang Su, loyal bluntness such as Qiang Zhen, and bright integrity such as Zhang Mao, Lin Jun, and Zhang Ji are the hope of the age. They should not be demoted and confined, betraying Heaven's intent in producing talent.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠召此數人，置要近之地，使各盡其平生，則天心協矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly summons these several men and places them in important and near positions, letting each exhaust his life's work, then Heaven's heart will be in accord.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly summons these men and places them in important posts near the throne, letting each fulfill his life's purpose, then Heaven's heart will be in accord.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞高皇帝制閽寺，惟給掃除，不及以政。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that the founding emperor regulated palace gatekeepers, giving them only sweeping and cleaning, not extending to government.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that the founding emperor regulated the palace eunuchs, assigning them only sweeping and cleaning, not government affairs.

sentences.zh: 近者舊章日壞，邪徑日開，人主大權盡出其手。

translations.literal: Recently old regulations daily decay and crooked paths daily open; the ruler's great power entirely issues from their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Recently old regulations have decayed daily and crooked paths opened daily; the ruler's great power has passed entirely into their hands.

sentences.zh: 內倚之為相，外倚之為將，藩方倚之為鎮撫，伶人賤工倚之以作奇技淫巧，法王佛子倚之以恣出入宮禁，此豈高皇帝所許哉！

translations.literal: Within they are relied on as chancellors, without as generals, in frontier regions as grand coordinators, low actors and base craftsmen rely on them to make strange skills and extravagant crafts, dharma kings and buddha sons rely on them to come and go at will in the palace forbidden precincts—is this what the founding emperor permitted!
translations.idiomatic: Within the court they are relied on as chancellors; without, as generals; in the provinces, as grand coordinators; actors and craftsmen rely on them for extravagant displays; Buddhist clerics rely on them to come and go freely within the palace precincts—is this what the founding emperor permitted?

sentences.zh: 願陛下以宰相為股肱，以諫官為耳目，以正人君子為腹心，深思極慮，定宗社長久之計，則大綱正矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take chancellors as arms and thighs, remonstrance officials as ears and eyes, upright gentlemen as belly and heart, think deeply and consider to the utmost, and fix a long-lasting plan for the altars of state—then the great norms will be correct.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty take chancellors as your arms and thighs, remonstrance officials as your ears and eyes, and upright gentlemen as your heart, think deeply, and fix a long-lasting plan for the altars of state—then the great norms will be set right.

sentences.zh: 然其本則在陛下明理何如耳。

translations.literal: Yet the root lies in how Your Majesty clarifies principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the root of it all lies in how clearly Your Majesty understands principle.

sentences.zh: 竊聞侍臣進講無反復論辨之功，陛下聽講亦無從容沃心之益。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when attending ministers lecture there is no effect of repeated discussion and debate, and when Your Majesty listens there is no benefit of leisurely nourishment of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when attending ministers lecture there is no real discussion or debate, and when Your Majesty listens there is no real benefit of nourishing the mind.

sentences.zh: 如此而欲明理以應事，臣不信也。

translations.literal: Wishing thus to clarify principle to respond to affairs—your subject does not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: To wish thus to clarify principle and respond to affairs—I cannot believe it possible.

sentences.zh: 願陛下念義理之難窮，惜日月之易邁，考之經史，驗之身心，使終歲無間，則聖學明而萬事畢治，豈特四事之舉措得其當已耶。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to reflect that principle is hard to exhaust, cherish that days and months easily pass, examine it in the classics and histories and test it in body and mind, making the whole year without interruption—then sagely learning will be clear and the myriad affairs all governed; is it only that the four affairs' measures will be fitting?
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty reflect that principle is hard to exhaust fully, cherish how swiftly the days pass, examine it in the classics and histories and test it in your own person without interruption through the year—then sagely learning will be clear and all affairs well governed. Will it be only these four matters that are set right?

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, no response was given.

sentences.zh: 智既慷慨負奇，其時御史湯鼐、中書舍人吉人、進士李文祥亦並負意氣，智皆與之善。

translations.literal: Zhi being generous and bearing exceptional talent, at the time Censor Tang Tai, Secretariat Drafter Ji Ren, and jinshi Li Wenxiang also all bore spirited resolve—Zhi was on good terms with them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was generous and possessed of exceptional talent. At the time Censor Tang Tai, Secretariat Drafter Ji Ren, and jinshi Li Wenxiang were also men of spirited resolve, and Zhi was on good terms with them all.

sentences.zh: 因相與品核公卿，裁量人物。

translations.literal: They accordingly together appraised dukes and ministers and measured men's characters.
translations.idiomatic: Together they appraised the senior officials and weighed men's characters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孝宗嗣位，弊政多所更。

translations.literal: Before long the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded to the throne, and many abusive policies were changed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded to the throne, and many abusive policies were reformed.

sentences.zh: 智喜，以為其誌且得行，乃復因星變上書曰：

translations.literal: Zhi rejoiced, thinking his aim would soon be carried out, and again on account of a stellar anomaly submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhi rejoiced, believing his aims would soon be realized, and again, on account of a stellar anomaly, submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 伏讀明詔雲「天下利弊所當興革，所在官員人等條具以聞」。

translations.literal: Your subject has read the clear edict which says: "Benefits and harms throughout the realm that ought to be raised or abolished—let officials everywhere itemize and report."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has read the clear edict stating, "Benefits and harms throughout the realm that ought to be raised or abolished—let officials everywhere itemize and report."

sentences.zh: 此殆陛下知前日登極詔書為奸臣所誤，禁言官毋風聞挾私言事，物論囂然，故復下此條自解耳。

translations.literal: This perhaps means Your Majesty knows the accession edict of the other day was misled by treacherous ministers, forbidding remonstrance officials from reporting hearsay and speaking on affairs with private motives—public discussion was clamorous—and therefore again issued this clause to explain yourself.
translations.idiomatic: This perhaps means Your Majesty knows the accession edict was misled by treacherous ministers when it forbade remonstrance officials from reporting hearsay and speaking with private motives—public discussion was clamorous—and therefore issued this clause to explain yourself.

sentences.zh: 夫不曰「朕躬有過，朝政有闕」，而曰「利弊當興革」；
