translations.literal: Rather than saying "My person has faults, court government has gaps," you say "benefits and harms ought to be raised and abolished";
translations.idiomatic: Rather than saying "My person has faults and court government has failings," you say "benefits and harms ought to be raised and abolished";

sentences.zh: 不曰「許諸人直言無隱」，而曰「官員人等條具以聞」。

translations.literal: rather than saying "I permit all men to speak directly without concealment," you say "let officials everywhere itemize and report."
translations.idiomatic: rather than saying "I permit all men to speak directly without concealment," you say "let officials everywhere itemize and report."

sentences.zh: 陛下所以求言者，已不廣矣。

translations.literal: The scope of Your Majesty's seeking words is already not broad.
translations.idiomatic: The scope of Your Majesty's invitation to speak is already narrow.

sentences.zh: 今欲興天下之利，革天下之弊，當求利弊之本原而興且革之，不當毛舉細故，以為利弊在是也。

translations.literal: Now wishing to raise the realm's benefits and abolish the realm's harms, one ought to seek the root source of benefits and harms and raise and abolish them—not pick out minor details and think benefits and harms lie there.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to raise the realm's benefits and abolish its harms, you must seek the root source of benefits and harms and act there—not pick out minor details and think the root lies in them.

sentences.zh: 本原何在？

translations.literal: Where is the root source?
translations.idiomatic: Where is the root source?

sentences.zh: 閣臣是已。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat ministers—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat ministers—that is where it lies.

sentences.zh: 少師安持祿怙寵，少保吉附下罔上，太子少保直挾詐懷奸，世之小人也。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor An clings to salary and relies on favor; Junior Guardian Ji fawns on subordinates and deceives superiors; Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Zhi harbors deceit and treachery—the petty men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor Wan An clings to salary and relies on favor; Junior Guardian Liu Ji fawns on subordinates and deceives superiors; Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhi harbors deceit and treachery—they are the petty men of the age.

sentences.zh: 陛下留之，則君德必不就，朝政必不修，此弊所當革者也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty keeps them, rulerly virtue will surely not be attained and court government will surely not be cultivated—this harm ought to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty keeps them, rulerly virtue will never be attained and court government will never be set right—this is the harm that must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 致仕尚書王恕忠亮可任大事，尚書王竑剛毅可寢大奸，都御史彭韶方正可決大疑，世之君子也。

translations.literal: Retired Minister Wang Su is loyal and bright and can undertake great affairs; Minister Wang Hong is firm and resolute and can put great traitors to rest; Censor-in-Chief Peng Shao is upright and can resolve great doubts—the gentlemen of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Minister Wang Su is loyal and bright and fit for great affairs; Minister Wang Hong is firm and resolute and can suppress great traitors; Censor-in-Chief Peng Shao is upright and can resolve great doubts—they are the gentlemen of the age.

sentences.zh: 陛上用之，則君德開明，朝政清肅，此利所當興也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty employs them, rulerly virtue will be enlightened and court government clear and solemn—this benefit ought to be raised.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty employs them, rulerly virtue will be enlightened and court government clear and solemn—this is the benefit that must be raised.

sentences.zh: 然君子所以不進，小人所以不退，大抵由宦官權重而已。

translations.literal: Yet why gentlemen do not advance and petty men do not withdraw is largely due to eunuchs' heavy power alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet why gentlemen do not advance and petty men do not withdraw is largely due to the eunuchs' heavy power.

sentences.zh: 漢元帝嘗任蕭望之、周堪矣，卒制於弘恭、石顯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Han once entrusted Xiao Wangzhi and Zhou Kan, yet in the end was controlled by Hong Gong and Shi Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Han once entrusted Xiao Wangzhi and Zhou Kan, yet in the end was controlled by the eunuchs Hong Gong and Shi Xian.

sentences.zh: 宋孝宗嘗任劉俊卿、劉珙矣，卒間於陳源、甘昇。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong of Song once entrusted Liu Junqing and Liu Gong, yet in the end was estranged by Chen Yuan and Gan Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong of Song once entrusted Liu Junqing and Liu Gong, yet in the end was estranged by the eunuchs Chen Yuan and Gan Sheng.

sentences.zh: 李林甫、牛仙客與高力士相附和，而唐政不綱。

translations.literal: Li Linfu and Niu Xianke echoed Gao Lishi, and Tang government lost its norms.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu and Niu Xianke echoed the eunuch Gao Lishi, and Tang government lost its norms.

sentences.zh: 賈似道、丁大全與董宋臣相表裏，而宋室不振。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao and Ding Daquan were inside and outside with Dong Songchen, and the Song house did not revive.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao and Ding Daquan worked hand in glove with Dong Songchen, and the Song house failed to revive.

sentences.zh: 君子小人進退之機，未嘗不系此曹之盛衰。

translations.literal: The occasion for gentlemen's advance and petty men's withdrawal has never not depended on whether this lot flourish or decline.
translations.idiomatic: Whether gentlemen advance and petty men withdraw has never failed to depend on whether such men flourish or decline.

sentences.zh: 願陛下鑒既往，謹將來，攬天綱，張英斷。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take warning from the past, be cautious about the future, gather Heaven's net, and extend heroic decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty take warning from the past, be cautious about the future, gather Heaven's authority, and exercise heroic decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 凡所以待宦官者，一以高皇帝為法，則君子可進，小人可退，而天下之治出於一矣。

translations.literal: In all ways of treating eunuchs, take the founding emperor alone as model—then gentlemen can advance, petty men can withdraw, and the realm's good government will issue from one source.
translations.idiomatic: In all your treatment of eunuchs, take the founding emperor alone as your model—then gentlemen can advance, petty men can withdraw, and good government will issue from a single source.

sentences.zh: 以陛下聰明冠世，豈不知刑臣不可委信，然而不免誤用者，殆正心之學未講也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's intelligence surpassing the age, would you not know that castrated ministers cannot be entrusted? Yet that you cannot avoid misusing them is perhaps because the learning of rectifying the heart has not been discussed.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's intelligence surpassing the age, would you not know that castrated ministers cannot be entrusted? Yet that you cannot avoid misusing them is perhaps because the learning of rectifying the heart has not been cultivated.

sentences.zh: 心發於天理，則耳目聰明，言動中節，何宦官之能惑。

translations.literal: When the heart issues from heavenly principle, then ears and eyes are clear and bright and words and actions hit the mark—how could eunuchs beguile?
translations.idiomatic: When the heart issues from heavenly principle, ears and eyes are clear and words and actions hit the mark—how could eunuchs beguile you?

sentences.zh: 發於人欲，則一身無主，萬事失綱，投間抵隙，蒙蔽得施。

translations.literal: When it issues from human desire, then the single person has no master, the myriad affairs lose their norm, and seizing gaps and striking openings, obscuring and covering can be applied.
translations.idiomatic: When it issues from human desire, the person has no master within, the myriad affairs lose their norm, and obscuring and deception find their opening.

sentences.zh: 雖有神武之資，亦將日改月化而浸失其初。

translations.literal: Even with divine martial endowment, one will daily change and monthly transform and gradually lose the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Even with divine martial endowment, one will daily change and monthly transform until the original purpose is gradually lost.

sentences.zh: 欲進君子退小人，興天下之利，革天下之弊，豈可得哉？

translations.literal: Wishing to advance gentlemen and retire petty men, raise the realm's benefits and abolish the realm's harms—how can it be attained?
translations.idiomatic: To wish to advance gentlemen and dismiss petty men, raise benefits and abolish harms throughout the realm—how can it be attained?

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial and nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial and nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 居無何，安、直相繼罷斥。

translations.literal: Before long, An and Zhi were successively dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Wan An and Yin Zhi were successively dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而吉任寄如故，銜智刺骨。

translations.literal: But Ji's entrustment remained as before, and he bore a grudge against Zhi to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Ji's power remained as before, and he bore a grudge against Zhi to the bone.

sentences.zh: 鼐常朝當侍班，智告之曰：「祖宗盛時，御史侍班，得面陳政務得失，立取進止。

translations.literal: Tai, when attending court, was on attendance duty; Zhi told him: "In the flourishing time of the ancestral emperors, censors on attendance duty could face the throne and state the gains and losses of government affairs, and immediately receive approval or rejection."
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Tai was on attendance duty at court, Zhi told him, "In the flourishing age of the ancestral emperors, censors on attendance duty could face the throne and state the gains and losses of government affairs, and immediately receive approval or rejection."

sentences.zh: 自後惟退而具疏，此君臣情意所由隔也。

translations.literal: Afterward they only withdrew and submitted memorials—this is how ruler and minister affection and intent came to be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they only withdrew and submitted written memorials—this is how affection and understanding between ruler and minister came to be severed.

sentences.zh: 君幸值維新之日，盍仿先朝故事行之。

translations.literal: You are fortunate to meet a day of renewal—why not imitate the former court's precedent and carry it out?
translations.idiomatic: You are fortunate to live in a day of renewal—why not imitate the former court's precedent and act on it?"

sentences.zh: 」及恕赴召至京，智往謁曰：「後世人臣不獲時見天子，故事多茍且。

translations.literal: " When Su, answering the summons, reached the capital, Zhi went to visit him and said: "Later-age ministers do not obtain timely audience with the Son of Heaven; precedents are mostly perfunctory."
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Su answered the summons and reached the capital, Zhi visited him and said, "Later-age ministers no longer obtain timely audience with the Son of Heaven, and precedents have become mostly perfunctory."

sentences.zh: 願公且勿受官，先請朝見，取時政不善者歷陳之，力請除革，而後拜命，庶其有濟。

translations.literal: I wish you for the moment not to accept office, first request audience, take what is ungood in current government and state them one by one, strongly request removal and reform, and only afterward accept appointment—perhaps there will be effect.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you not to accept office yet. First request audience, enumerate what is wrong in current government, strongly urge removal and reform, and only then accept appointment—perhaps something can be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 若先受官，無復見天子之日矣。

translations.literal: If you first accept office, there will be no more days of seeing the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If you accept office first, you will never again have a day to see the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」鼐與恕亦未能用其言。

translations.literal: " Tai and Su also could not use his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Neither Tang Tai nor Wang Su could act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 會劉概獄起，吉使其黨魏璋入智名，遂下詔獄。

translations.literal: When the Liu Gai case arose, Ji had his faction-member Wei Zhang insert Zhi's name, and he was sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu Gai case arose, Liu Ji had his follower Wei Zhang insert Zhi's name, and Zhi was sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 智身親三木，僅屬喘息，慷慨對簿曰：「智見經筵以寒暑輟講，午朝以細事塞責，紀綱廢馳，風俗浮薄，生民憔悴，邊備空虛，私竊以為憂。

translations.literal: Zhi personally wore the three woods, barely able to breathe, and said generously at trial: "Zhi has seen the classics lecture halted through cold and heat, the noon audience blocked with petty affairs to fulfill duty, norms abandoned and neglected, customs shallow and thin, the living people haggard, frontier defense empty—I privately thought this a worry."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wore the cangue in person and could barely breathe, yet said generously at trial, "I have seen the classics lecture halted through cold and heat, the noon audience blocked with petty affairs, norms abandoned, customs shallow, the people haggard, and frontier defense empty—I privately took this as cause for worry."

sentences.zh: 與鼐等往來論議誠有之，不知其他。

translations.literal: That I exchanged discussions with Tai and the others is truly so; I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: It is true that I exchanged discussions with Tang Tai and others; I know nothing beyond that."

sentences.zh: 」讞者承吉意，竟謫廣東石城所吏目，事具《湯鼐傳》。

translations.literal: " The legal reporter followed Ji's intent and in the end demoted him to Clerk of the Shicheng Guard in Guangdong; the affair is fully recorded in the "Biography of Tang Tai."
translations.idiomatic: " The legal reporter followed Liu Ji's intent and in the end demoted him to clerk of the Shicheng Guard in Guangdong; the affair is fully recorded in the Biography of Tang Tai.

sentences.zh: 智至廣東，總督秦纮檄召修書，乃居會城。

translations.literal: When Zhi reached Guangdong, Grand Coordinator Qin Hong summoned him by order to compile books, and he then resided in the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi reached Guangdong, Grand Coordinator Qin Hong summoned him by order to compile books, and he resided in the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 聞陳獻章講道新會，往受業，自是學益粹。

translations.literal: Hearing that Chen Xianzhang lectured on the Way at Xinhui, he went to receive instruction; from this his learning grew purer.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Chen Xianzhang was teaching the Way at Xinhui, he went to study under him; from then on his learning grew purer still.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年十月得疾遽卒，年二十有六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Hongzhi he fell ill and died suddenly, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Hongzhi 4 he took ill and died abruptly at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 同年生吳廷舉為順德知縣，殮而歸其喪。

translations.literal: His fellow jinshi of the same year, Wu Tingju, was magistrate of Shunde; he prepared the body for burial and escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingju, who had passed the jinshi examination in the same year, was serving as magistrate of Shunde County; he prepared the body for burial and sent the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚忠介。

translations.literal: In the early Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the honorific title Zhongjie ("Loyal and Upright").
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign the court posthumously honored him with the title Zhongjie ("Loyal and Upright").

sentences.zh: 舒芬，字國裳，進賢人。

translations.literal: Shu Fen, courtesy name Guoshang, was a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Fen, styled Guoshang, came from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 年十二，獻《馴雁賦》於知府祝瀚，遂知名。

translations.literal: At age twelve he presented "Ode on the Tame Wild Geese" to Prefect Zhu Han and thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve he submitted his "Ode on the Tame Wild Geese" to Prefect Zhu Han and gained a reputation for his talent.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年舉進士第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he ranked first among jinshi graduates and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 12 he came in first on the jinshi examination and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時武宗數微行，畋遊無度。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wuzong frequently went out incognito, hunting and roaming without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Wuzong often slipped out in disguise on hunting excursions with no limit.

sentences.zh: 其明年，孝貞皇后崩甫逾月，欲幸宣府。

translations.literal: The next year, barely a month after Empress Xiaozhen's death, he wished to travel to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, scarcely a month after Empress Xiaozhen had died, he wanted to visit Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 托言往視山陵，罷沿道兵衛。

translations.literal: He claimed he was going to inspect the imperial tombs and dismissed the military guards along the route.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext of visiting the imperial tombs, he disbanded the military escorts posted along the road.

sentences.zh: 芬上言：「陛下三年之內當深居不出，雖釋服之後，固儼然煢疚也。

translations.literal: Fen submitted a memorial: "Within the three-year mourning period Your Majesty ought to remain in deep seclusion and not go abroad; even after the end of mourning garb, you should still appear solemnly bereft and mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Feng submitted a memorial stating: "Your Majesty should remain in deep seclusion throughout the three-year mourning period; even after shedding mourning dress, you ought to continue to bear the solemn air of one who has lost a parent.

sentences.zh: 且自古萬乘之重，非奔竄逃匿，未有不嚴侍衛者。

translations.literal: Moreover, since antiquity the weight of the imperial chariot has never lacked strict guards, except when one is fleeing in panic or hiding in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, from ancient times no ruler of the realm has ever traveled without a strict guard, unless he were running away or in hiding.

sentences.zh: 又等威莫大於車服，以天子之尊下同庶人，舍大輅袞冕而羸車褻服是禦，非所以辨上下、定禮儀。

translations.literal: Furthermore, no emblem of rank is greater than carriage and attire; to place the Son of Heaven's dignity on the same level as commoners, abandoning the great carriage and court robes to ride in a lean carriage in informal dress—this is not the way to distinguish high from low and establish ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, nothing defines rank more clearly than carriage and dress. For the Son of Heaven to travel like a commoner—discarding the imperial carriage and court robes for a lean cart and casual garments—is no way to distinguish rank or uphold ritual order.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: The memorial was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 孝貞山陵畢，迎主祔廟，自長安門入。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaozhen's tomb rites were completed, her spirit tablet was escorted to the ancestral temple for enshrinement, entering through Chang'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Xiaozhen's burial was complete, her spirit tablet was brought to the ancestral temple for enshrinement, entering through Chang'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 芬又言：「孝貞皇后作配茂陵，未聞失德。

translations.literal: Fen again stated: "Empress Xiaozhen was matched with Maoling; no misconduct has ever been heard of her.
translations.idiomatic: Feng submitted another memorial: "Empress Xiaozhen was properly paired with Emperor Xiaozong at Maoling, and no fault was ever attributed to her.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之制，既葬迎主，必入正門。

translations.literal: According to ancestral institution, after burial when escorting the spirit tablet, one must enter through the main gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under the institutions of our forefathers, when a spirit tablet is escorted home after burial, it must enter through the main gate.

sentences.zh: 昨孝貞之主，顧從陛下駕由旁門入，他日史臣書之曰「六月己丑，車駕至自山陵，迎孝貞純皇后主入長安門」，將使孝貞有不得正終之嫌，其何以解於天下後世？

translations.literal: Yesterday Empress Xiaozhen's tablet followed Your Majesty's carriage and entered by a side gate; someday when the historiographer writes, 'On the day jichou of the sixth month, the imperial carriage returned from the tombs and escorted the spirit tablet of the Pure Empress Xiaozhen into Chang'an Gate,' it will leave the suspicion that Empress Xiaozhen did not meet a proper end—how can this be explained to all under Heaven and to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Empress Xiaozhen's tablet entered by a side gate at Your Majesty's side. When future historians record that 'On the day jichou of the sixth month, the imperial carriage returned from the tombs and escorted the spirit tablet of the Pure Empress Xiaozhen into Chang'an Gate,' Empress Xiaozhen will be left under the suspicion of an improper end. How will that be explained to the world and to posterity?

sentences.zh: 昨祔廟之夕，疾風迅雷甚雨，意者聖祖列宗及孝貞皇后之靈，儆告陛下也。

translations.literal: On the night of the enshrinement, fierce wind, thunderclaps, and violent rain—perhaps the spirits of the holy ancestors and Empress Xiaozhen were issuing a warning to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the enshrinement there were violent winds, thunder, and torrential rain—perhaps the spirits of the dynastic founders and Empress Xiaozhen were warning Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜即明詔中外，以示改過。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought immediately to issue a clear edict to the court and the realm to show that you have corrected your error.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should at once issue a public edict to the court and the realm, demonstrating repentance.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 遂乞歸養，不許。

translations.literal: He then requested leave to return home to support his parents, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to resign and return home to care for his parents, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 又明年三月，帝議南巡。

translations.literal: Again the next year, in the third month, the Emperor deliberated a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the third month, the emperor proposed a southern tour.

sentences.zh: 時寧王宸濠久蓄異謀，與近幸相結，人情惶懼。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao had long harbored rebellious designs and was allied with those favored near the throne; public sentiment was fearful and anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao had long been nursing treasonous ambitions and had allied himself with the emperor's favorites; anxiety ran high among the people.

sentences.zh: 言官伏闕諫，忤旨被責讓。

translations.literal: Censorial officials prostrated themselves at the palace gate to remonstrate; defying the imperial will, they were reproved and rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials knelt at the palace gate to remonstrate; they defied the emperor's wishes and were rebuked and punished.

sentences.zh: 芬憂之，與吏部員外郎夏良勝、禮部主事萬潮、庶吉士汪應軫要諸曹連章入諫，眾許諾。

translations.literal: Fen was troubled by this and, together with Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xia Liangsheng, Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Wan Chao, and Junior Compiler Wang Yingzhen, urged the various bureaus to submit joint memorials of remonstrance; the crowd assented.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed by this, Feng joined Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xia Liangsheng, Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Wan Chao, and Junior Compiler Wang Yingzhen in urging officials across the ministries to submit joint remonstrance memorials; they all agreed.

sentences.zh: 芬遂偕編修崔桐，庶吉士江暉、王廷陳、馬汝驥、曹嘉及應軫上疏曰：

translations.literal: Fen then joined Compiler Cui Tong, Junior Compilers Jiang Hui, Wang Tingchen, Ma Ruji, and Cao Jia, together with Yingzhen, in submitting a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Feng then joined Compiler Cui Tong, Junior Compilers Jiang Hui, Wang Tingchen, Ma Ruji, and Cao Jia, along with Wang Yingzhen, in submitting a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「古帝王所以巡狩者，協律度，同量衡，訪遺老，問疾苦，黜陟幽明，式序在位，是以諸侯畏焉，百姓安焉。

translations.literal: Ancient emperors and kings undertook tours of inspection in order to harmonize standards of pitch and measure, unify weights and measures, visit elderly worthies, inquire into hardship and suffering, promote the obscure and demote the unworthy, and thereby put officials in their proper order—thus the feudal lords held them in awe and the common people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sovereigns toured the realm to harmonize musical pitch and measure, unify weights and measures, seek out elders of merit, inquire into the people's suffering, promote the worthy and dismiss the unworthy, and thereby put officials in proper order—so that the feudal lords stood in awe and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 若陛下之出，不過如秦皇、漢武，侈心為樂而已，非能行巡狩之禮者也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty's going forth is nothing more than like Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi, with a heart bent on extravagance and pleasure, it cannot be considered carrying out the rites of a tour of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's journey is no more than Qin Shihuang's or Han Wudi's excursions—indulgence pursued for pleasure—it cannot be called performing the rites of a tour of inspection.

sentences.zh: 博浪、柏谷，其禍亦可鑒矣。

translations.literal: Bolang and Baigu—the disasters there may also serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The disasters at Bolang and Baigu should serve as warnings.

sentences.zh: 近者西北再巡，六師不攝，四民告病。

translations.literal: Recently on two tours to the northwest, the armies were not kept in order and the four classes of people cried out in distress.
translations.idiomatic: On Your Majesty's two recent northwestern tours, military discipline collapsed and people of every walk of life were driven to despair.

sentences.zh: 哀痛之聲，上徹蒼昊。

translations.literal: Sounds of grief and anguish reached up to the azure heavens.
translations.idiomatic: The cries of grief rose all the way to heaven.

sentences.zh: 傳播四方，人心震動。

translations.literal: It spread in all four directions, and hearts were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The tidings spread in every direction, and public morale was shaken.

sentences.zh: 故一聞南巡詔書，皆鳥驚獸散。

translations.literal: Therefore, as soon as the edict for the southern tour was heard, everyone scattered like startled birds and fleeing beasts.
translations.idiomatic: So at the first rumor of a southern tour edict, people fled in panic like birds startled from the brush.

sentences.zh: 而有司方以迎奉為名，征發嚴急，江、淮之間蕭然煩費。

translations.literal: Yet the officials were just then levying labor in the name of receiving and serving the emperor, with urgent and severe demands; between the Yangzi and Huai there was desolation and exhausting expense.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile officials were requisitioning labor under the pretext of preparing to welcome the emperor, with brutal urgency; between the Yangzi and the Huai the land was stripped bare and the people exhausted.

sentences.zh: 萬一不逞之徒，乘勢倡亂，為禍非細。

translations.literal: Should unruly persons seize the opportunity to incite rebellion, the harm would not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If lawless elements seize the chance to stir up trouble, the consequences could be grave.

sentences.zh: 且陛下以鎮國公自命，茍至親王國境，或據勛臣之禮以待陛下，將北向朝之乎，抑南面受其朝乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, since Your Majesty styles himself Duke of Zhenguo, if he reaches the territory of an imperial prince, and the prince receives him according to the rites due a meritorious minister, will Your Majesty face north to pay court to him, or face south and receive his obeisance?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Your Majesty has taken the title Duke of Zhenguo, should you enter a prince's domain and find him receiving you with the honors owed a meritorious minister—will you bow north to pay him court, or sit facing south and accept his homage?

sentences.zh: 假令循名責實，深求悖謬之端，則左右寵幸無死所矣。

translations.literal: If one were to follow the name and demand the reality, deeply seeking out the root of perversity, then the favorites at Your Majesty's side would have no place to die.
translations.idiomatic: If the title were held to its true meaning and the contradictions traced to their source, Your Majesty's favored courtiers would have nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 尚有事堪痛哭不忍言者：宗藩蓄劉氵鼻之釁，大臣懷馮道之心。

translations.literal: There are still matters worth weeping over that one cannot bear to speak of: imperial clansmen harbor the seeds of rebellion like Liu Bei, and great ministers harbor hearts like Feng Dao's.
translations.idiomatic: There are matters so grievous one can scarcely speak of them: princes of the blood are nursing ambitions like Liu Bei's, and senior ministers carry the unprincipled opportunism of a Feng Dao.

sentences.zh: 以祿位為故物，以朝署為市廛，以陛下為弈棋，以革除年間為故事。

translations.literal: They treat salary and rank as old possessions, treat the court offices as a marketplace, treat Your Majesty as a piece on a chessboard, and treat the events of the Gengchu years as precedent to be followed.
translations.idiomatic: They treat office and emolument as personal property, the halls of government as a marketplace, Your Majesty as a chess piece, and the disorders of the Removing-the-Evil years as a model to repeat.

sentences.zh: 特左右寵幸知術短淺，無能以此言告陛下耳。

translations.literal: It is only that the favorites at Your Majesty's side, knowing their own schemes to be shallow and limited, are unable to report such words to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's court favorites simply will not relay such warnings—their own plots are too crude, and they lack either the wit or the will to speak.

sentences.zh: 使陛下得聞此言，雖禁門之外，亦將警蹕而出，尚敢輕騎慢遊哉？」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty could hear these words, even beyond the Forbidden Gate you would hasten out under full guard—how could you still dare to ride lightly and roam at leisure?"
translations.idiomatic: Were Your Majesty to hear such words, you would bolt from the palace even under full armed escort—how then could you still dare to ride out lightly for pleasure?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，陸完迎謂曰：「上聞有諫者輒恚，欲自引決。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Lu Wan met them and said: "When His Majesty hears there are remonstrators he grows enraged and wants to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Lu Wan intercepted them saying: "The Emperor grows furious whenever he hears of remonstrance and threatens to harm himself.

sentences.zh: 諸君且休，勿歸過君上，沽直名。

translations.literal: Gentlemen, desist for now; do not lay the blame on your sovereign or seek a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen, stop now. Do not blame the sovereign or seek to burnish your names for integrity.

sentences.zh: 」芬等不應而出。

translations.literal: Fen and the others made no reply and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng and his companions said nothing and left.

sentences.zh: 有頃，良勝、潮過芬，扼腕恨完。

translations.literal: Before long, Liangsheng and Chao passed by Fen, wringing their wrists in resentment against Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Xia Liangsheng and Wan Chao passed Feng, wringing their hands in anger at Lu Wan.

sentences.zh: 芬因邀博士陳九川至，酌之酒曰：「匹夫不可奪誌，君輩可遂已乎？

translations.literal: Fen then invited Doctor Chen Jiuchuan, poured him wine, and said: "A common man cannot be made to abandon his resolve—can you gentlemen simply let this stop here?
translations.idiomatic: Feng then invited Doctor Chen Jiuchuan, poured him wine, and said: "A resolute man will not be swayed from his purpose—can you really leave matters here?

sentences.zh: 」明日遂偕諸曹連疏入。

translations.literal: The next day they jointly submitted linked memorials from the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they and officials from across the ministries submitted joint memorials together.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命跪闕下五日，期滿復杖之三十。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and ordered them to kneel beneath the palace gate for five days; when the period expired they were again beaten with thirty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered them to kneel at the palace gate for five days; when that period ended, each received thirty blows with the beating staff.

sentences.zh: 芬創甚，幾斃，舁至翰林院中。

translations.literal: Fen's wounds were severe; he nearly died and was carried into the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was badly injured, near death, and was carried into the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 掌院者懼得罪，命摽出之，芬曰：「吾官此，即死此耳。

translations.literal: The academy director, fearing he would be implicated in guilt, ordered him carried out; Fen said, "My office is here—I shall die here.
translations.idiomatic: The academy's director, fearing punishment, ordered him removed; Feng said, "I hold my office here; if I must die, I shall die here.

sentences.zh: 」竟謫福建市舶副提舉，裹創就道。

translations.literal: In the end he was demoted to Vice Supervisor of the Fujian Maritime Trade Office and set out on the road with his wounds bound.
translations.idiomatic: He was ultimately demoted to Vice Supervisor of the Fujian Maritime Trade Office and departed for his post with his wounds still bandaged.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召復故官。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he was recalled and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Feng was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年春，昭聖太后壽旦，詔免諸命婦朝賀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Jiajing, on the birthday of Empress Dowager Zhaosheng, an edict exempted all titled ladies from attending court to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jiajing 3, on Empress Dowager Zhaosheng's birthday, an edict exempted titled ladies from the customary court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 芬言：「前者興國太后令旦，命婦朝賀如儀。

translations.literal: Fen stated: "Previously, on Empress Dowager Xingguo's birthday, titled ladies attended court to congratulate according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Feng argued: "When Empress Dowager Xingguo's birthday was observed, titled ladies congratulated her according to established ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今遇皇太后壽節，忽行傳免，恐失輕重之宜。

translations.literal: Now, encountering the Empress Dowager's birthday, an exemption has suddenly been announced—I fear this fails to preserve the proper balance of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the Empress Dowager's birthday, a sudden exemption has been announced, which I fear disrupts the proper balance of ceremonial honor.

sentences.zh: 乞收成命，以彰聖孝。

translations.literal: I beg that the edict be withdrawn to manifest sacred filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this order be revoked so that Your Majesty's filial reverence may be made clear.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，奪俸三月。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and withheld his salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and docked his pay for three months.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲尊崇本生，芬偕其僚連章極諫。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor wished to honor his biological father; Fen joined his colleagues in successive memorials of fierce remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sought to elevate his biological father in rank, Feng and his colleagues submitted a stream of vehement memorials in opposition.

sentences.zh: 及張璁、桂萼、方獻夫驟擢學士，芬及同官楊維聰、編修王思羞與同列，拜疏乞罷。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu were suddenly promoted to Grand Secretaries, Fen, his colleague Yang Weicong, and Compiler Wang Si, ashamed to serve alongside them, submitted memorials requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu were abruptly elevated to Hanlin academicians, Feng, his colleague Yang Weicong, and Compiler Wang Si—ashamed to serve alongside them—submitted memorials asking to resign.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復偕同官楊慎等伏左順門哭爭。

translations.literal: Before long, he again joined his colleagues Yang Shen and others in prostrating themselves at the Left Shun Gate, weeping and disputing.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he again joined Yang Shen and other colleagues in kneeling and weeping at the Left Shun Gate to protest.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下獄廷杖，奪俸如初。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered, had them imprisoned and beaten at court, and withheld salary as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, had them imprisoned and subjected to court beating, and again docked Feng's pay for three months.

sentences.zh: 旋遭母喪歸，卒於家，年四十四。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he met with his mother's death and returned home; he died at home, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned home upon his mother's death and died there at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 世稱「忠孝狀元」。

translations.literal: The age called him the "Loyal and Filial Zhuangyuan."
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries called him the "Loyal and Filial Zhuangyuan."

sentences.zh: 芬豐神玉立，負氣峻厲，端居竟日無倦容，夜則計過自訟。

translations.literal: Fen's bearing was imposing like jade standing upright; he possessed stern and fierce spirit. Sitting in repose all day he showed no weariness; at night he counted his faults and reproached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Feng carried himself with the upright grace of polished jade and a fierce, unyielding spirit. He could sit in meditation all day without fatigue, and at night he would review his faults and rebuke himself.

sentences.zh: 以倡明絕學為己任。

translations.literal: He took it as his personal mission to promote and elucidate the supreme learning.
translations.idiomatic: He made it his life's work to revive and champion the highest scholarship.

sentences.zh: 其學貫串諸經，兼通天文律歷，而尤精於《周禮》。

translations.literal: His learning threaded through all the classics; he was also versed in astronomy, pitch pipes, and calendrical reckoning, and was especially expert in the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship spanned the entire canon; he also mastered astronomy, pitch standards, and calendrical science, and was especially expert in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「《周禮》視《儀禮》、《禮記》，猶蜀之視吳、魏也。

translations.literal: He once said: "The Rites of Zhou compared to the Ceremonial Rites and the Record of Rites is like Shu viewing Wu and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked: "The Rites of Zhou stands toward the Ceremonial Rites and the Record of Rites as Shu stands toward Wu and Wei"—that is, as the true inheritor of legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 賈氏謂《儀禮》為本，《周禮》為末，妄矣。

translations.literal: Master Jia said the Ceremonial Rites was the root and the Rites of Zhou was the branch—this is absurd.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Gong said the Ceremonial Rites was fundamental and the Rites of Zhou derivative, he was simply wrong.

sentences.zh: 朱子不加是正，何也？

translations.literal: Why did Master Zhu not correct this?
translations.idiomatic: Why did Zhu Xi never set the record straight?

sentences.zh: 」疾革，其子請所言，惟以未及表章《周禮》為恨。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, his son asked what he wished to say; he spoke only of regretting that he had not yet been able to expound and glorify the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he was dying, his son asked if he had any final words; he replied only that he regretted not having completed his exposition of the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 學者稱「梓溪先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars called him "Master Zixi."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honored him as "Master Zixi."

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，追謚文節。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he was posthumously granted the honorific Wenjie ("Cultured and Principled").
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign the court posthumously honored him with the title Wenjie ("Cultured and Principled").

sentences.zh: 先是，修撰羅倫以諫謫福建提舉，逾六十年而芬繼之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Compiler Luo Lun had been demoted to Fujian Intendant for remonstrance; more than sixty years later Fen followed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Decades earlier, Compiler Luo Lun had been banished to the Fujian Intendant post for remonstrating; more than sixty years later Feng suffered the same fate.

sentences.zh: 與倫同鄉同官，所謫地與官又同，福建士大夫遂祀芬配倫雲。

translations.literal: He was from the same home district and held the same office as Luo; the place and office of demotion were also the same, so the Fujian scholar-officials enshrined Fen alongside Luo at the Yun shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He shared Luo Lun's home district and official rank, and his place of exile and position were identical; Fujian scholar-officials therefore enshrined Feng alongside Luo at the Yun shrine.

sentences.zh: 崔桐，字來鳳，海門人。

translations.literal: Cui Tong, courtesy name Laifeng, was a native of Haimen.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tong, styled Laifeng, came from Haimen.

sentences.zh: 鄉試第一，與芬同進士及第。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the provincial examination and passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Fen.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the provincial examinations and received his jinshi degree in the same year as Feng.

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 既諫南巡，並跪闕下，受杖奪俸。

translations.literal: Having remonstrated against the southern tour, he knelt together beneath the palace gate, was beaten with the staff, and had his salary confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: After joining the southern tour remonstrance, he knelt at the palace gate with the others, was beaten, and had his salary docked.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，以侍讀出為湖廣右參議，累擢國子祭酒，禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign he left office as Reader and became Right Assistant Commissioner of Huguang; he was successively promoted to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy and Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he went out from his Reader post to serve as Right Assistant Commissioner of Huguang, then rose through the ranks to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy and Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 馬汝驥，字仲房，綏德人。

translations.literal: Ma Ruji, courtesy name Zhongfang, was a native of Suide.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ruji, styled Zhongfang, came from Suide.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi graduate in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Junior Compiler.

sentences.zh: 偕芬等諫南巡，罰跪受杖。

translations.literal: Together with Fen and others he remonstrated against the southern tour, was punished by kneeling and beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Feng and others in remonstrating against the southern tour and was punished with kneeling and beating.

sentences.zh: 教習期滿，當授編修，特調澤州知州。

translations.literal: When his term of instruction expired he should have been appointed Compiler, but was specially transferred to be Prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his Junior Compiler term ended he should have been promoted to Compiler, but was instead posted as prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 懲王府人虐小民。

translations.literal: He punished persons of the princely mansion who abused common people.
translations.idiomatic: He punished members of the princely household who mistreated commoners.

sentences.zh: 比王有所屬，輒投其書櫝中不視。

translations.literal: Whenever the prince had some assignment for him, he would throw the document into his document box and not look at it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince sent him instructions, he tossed the documents into his desk box unread.

sentences.zh: 陵川知縣貪，汝驥欲黜之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Lingchuan was corrupt; Ruji wished to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Lingchuan was corrupt, and Ma Ruji sought to remove him from office.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史為曲解，汝驥不聽，竟褫其官。

translations.literal: The touring censor offered a lenient interpretation, but Ruji would not listen and in the end stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor tried to smooth matters over, but Ma Ruji would not hear of it and ultimately stripped the man of his post.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，召復編修，尋錄直諫功，增秩一等。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he was recalled and restored as Compiler; soon his merit in direct remonstrance was recorded and his rank was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Ma Ruji was recalled as Compiler; shortly afterward his bold remonstrance was officially recognized and his rank was raised one step.

sentences.zh: 預修《武宗實錄》，進修撰。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Wuzong and was promoted to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong and was promoted to Compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京國子司業，擢南京右通政，就改國子祭酒，召拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Chancellor of the Imperial Academy in both capitals, was promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of the Nanking Secretariat, was then changed to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Chancellor of the Imperial Academy in both capitals, was promoted to Right Vice Commissioner in Nanjing, transferred to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and was then summoned as Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尚書嚴嵩愛重汝驥，入閣稱之，帝特加侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Minister Yan Song held Ruji in affection and esteem; entering the Grand Secretariat he praised him, and the Emperor specially added to him the title Reader of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yan Song held Ma Ruji in high regard; when Yan entered the Grand Secretariat he recommended him, and the emperor specially added for him the title Grand Secretariat Reader.

sentences.zh: 汝驥行己峭厲，然性故和易，人望歸焉。

translations.literal: Ruji in his conduct was stern and severe, yet by nature he was easygoing and amiable; public esteem gathered upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ruji was rigorous in his personal conduct yet naturally warm and approachable, and he commanded wide respect.

sentences.zh: 卒贈尚書，謚文簡。

translations.literal: Upon death he was posthumously granted the title of Minister and the honorific Wenjian ("Cultured and Simple").
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as Minister and given the title Wenjian ("Cultured and Simple").

sentences.zh: 應軫等自有傳。

translations.literal: Yingzhen and others have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingzhen and the others are given separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：詞臣以文學侍從為職，非有言責也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Literary officials take as their duty to attend in literary service; they have no mandate to speak out in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler writes: Literary officials serve by attending on the emperor with learning and letters; remonstrance is not their assigned duty.

sentences.zh: 激於名義，侃侃廷諍，抵罪謫而不悔，豈非皎然誌節之士歟？

translations.literal: Stirred by reputation and principle, speaking forthrightly in court remonstrance, meeting punishment and demotion without regret—are they not men of brilliantly manifest resolution and integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Yet stirred by moral duty, they remonstrated boldly at court, accepted punishment and exile without regret—were they not men of unmistakable integrity?

sentences.zh: 奪情之典不始李賢，然自羅倫疏傳誦天下，而朝臣不敢以起復為故事，於倫理所裨，豈淺鮮哉。

translations.literal: The institution of seizing from mourning did not begin with Li Xian, yet from the time Luo Lun's memorial was recited throughout the realm, court ministers no longer dared to treat recall from mourning as routine precedent—the benefit to human relations and principle, how could it be slight?
translations.idiomatic: The practice of compelling officials to leave mourning early did not begin with Li Xian, but after Luo Lun's memorial circulated nationwide, court officials no longer treated recall from filial mourning as routine precedent—a moral gain of no small consequence.

sentences.zh: 章懋等引宣宗箴，明國家設官意，不為彰君之過。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao and others cited Emperor Xuanzong's admonition, clarifying the intent behind the state's establishment of offices—they did not seek to expose the ruler's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao and others cited Emperor Xuanzong's admonitions to clarify the purpose for which the state establishes offices—not to parade the monarch's errors before the world.

sentences.zh: 鄒智指列賢奸，矯拂俞末。

translations.literal: Zou Zhi pointed out the worthy and the wicked, rectifying and guiding from the foundation to the finest points.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhi named the worthy and the wicked alike, correcting conduct from root to branch down to the smallest detail.

sentences.zh: 舒芬危言聳切，有爰盎攬轡之風。

translations.literal: Shu Fen's stern words were alarming and cutting, bearing the air of Yuan Ang reining in the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Fen spoke with alarming bluntness, in the spirit of Yuan Ang taking the reins in hand.

sentences.zh: 況夫清修峻節，行無瑕尤，若諸子者，洵足以矯文士浮誇之習矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, with pure cultivation and stern integrity, conduct without flaw or fault—men such as these are truly sufficient to correct the literary scholars' habit of empty exaggeration.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with pure conduct, stern integrity, and lives without blemish, men such as these were truly fit to correct the literary scholars' habit of empty display.
